( C [ a , b ] , dist ) 中的任意 Cauchy 序列 { f n ​ } 都收敛于某个 f ∈ C [ a , b ] , 因此 ( C [ a , b ] , dist ) 是完备度量空间. □ 3. 试题：几何群论 1 25-26 秋期末 (伍晓磊) 说明: 25-26 秋季学期的几何群论课程授课老师为伍晓磊老师, 教材为 Petra Schwer 的 CAT(0) Cube Complexes - An Introduction, 但是此教材错误过多, 伍老师说之后再开课的话可能会改教材. 考试形式为口试, 每人 20 分钟, 可选择中文或英文回答 (选择用英文则会有一个外国助教一起听然后和伍老师商量给分, 如果用中文则由伍老师一人给分) , 以下为部分口试题目. 1. 给出度量空间和测地空间的定义. 2. (1) 给出 CAT(0) 空间的定义. (2) 为什么 CAT(0) 空间中测地三角形的比较三角形一定存在? (3) 证明 CAT(0) 空间是唯一测地的. 3. (1) 给出群的 Cayley 图的定义. (2) 给出一个群的 Cayley 图是 CAT(0) 空间的例子并证明. (3) (因为我上一问回答了 F 2 ​ 并用 Gromov’s Link Condition 给出证明, 因此追加这一问及下面一问) 给出一个单纯复形是 flag 的定义. (4) 一个有限生成的群的 Cayley 图一定是局部 CAT(0) 的吗? (5) 如果一个群的 Cayley 图是 CAT(0) 的, 更换生成集得到的新 Cayley 图一定还是 CAT(0) 的吗? (答案为否, 考虑 Z = ⟨ 2 , 3 ⟩ ) (6) 一个有限生成群的 Cayley 图有什么特征是不随生成集改变而改变的? 4. (1) 给出 Coxeter 群的定义. (2) 两个 Coxeter 群的直积还是 Coxeter 群吗? 两个 Coxeter 群的自由积还是 Coxeter 群吗? (3) 如果一个 Coxeter 群的 Coxeter 图只有两个顶点, 那么这个群具有什么样的形式? 它可以 properly discontinuous 地等距作用在什么样的 CAT(0) cube complex 上?

T 有循环向量的充要条件是其特征多项式没有重根. 判断: 假. 解析: 线性变换 T 有循环向量的充要条件是其最小多项式等于特征多项式 (即特征矩阵的各阶不变因子中只有一个不为 1 ) . 特征多项式无重根只是一个充分条件 (此时特征值互异, 最小多项式必等于特征多项式) . 反例: 考虑矩阵 J = ( λ 0 ​ 1 λ ​ ) , 其特征多项式为 ( x − λ ) 2 , 有重根, 但其最小多项式也是 ( x − λ ) 2 , 它存在循环向量 (例如 ( 0 , 1 ) T ) . 2. 半正定实对称阵的特征值全部是非负实数. 判断: 真. 解析: 实对称阵必可正交对角化, 其特征值均为实数. 设 λ 为半正定实对称阵 A 的任一特征值, α  = 0 为对应的特征向量, 则 A α = λ α . 由半正定性可知 α T A α ≥ 0 , 即 α T ( λ α ) = λ α T α ≥ 0 . 因为 α  = 0 , 所以 α T α > 0 , 从而推出 λ ≥ 0 . 3. 若 f 是非退化对称双线性型, V 0 ​ 是 V 的子空间, 则 V = V 0 ​ ⊕ V 0 ⊥ ​ . 判断: 假. 解析: 该命题成立的条件是 f 在子空间 V 0 ​ 上的限制也必须是非退化的. 如果 f 存在非零的迷向向量 (如在闵可夫斯基空间中) , 则可能出现 V 0 ​ ∩ V 0 ⊥ ​  = { 0 } 的情况. 例如, 取 V = R 2 × 1 , f 在标准基下的矩阵为 ( 1 0 ​ 0 − 1 ​ ) , V 0 ​ = span {( 1 , 1 ) T } . 此时对于 α ∈ V 0 ​ , f ( α , α ) = 1 − 1 = 0 , 即 V 0 ​ ⊆ V 0 ⊥ ​ , 两者无法构成直和. 4. 若 f 是反对称双线性型, 则 d i m V 是偶数. 判断: 假. 解析: 只有当 f 是 非退化 的反对称双线性型 (即辛形式) 时, 空间的维数才必须是偶数. 如果 f 是退化的 (例如零双线性型) , 它可以定义在任意维数 (包括奇数维) 的向量空间上. 5. 幂零阵的 Jordan 标准型中的 Jordan 块个数等于该矩阵的零空间的维数. 判断: 真. 解析: 对于任意方阵 A , 属于特征值 λ 的 Jordan 块的个数等于该特征值的几何重数, 即 dim Ker ( A − λ I ) . 由于幂零阵的唯一特征值是 0 , 所以其 Jordan 块的个数严格等于 dim Ker ( A ) , 即零空间的维数. 6. V ⊗ W = { α ⊗ β ∣ α ∈ V , β ∈ W } . 判断: 假. 解析: 集合 { α ⊗ β ∣ α ∈ V , β ∈ W } 只是张量积空间中的 单张量 (simple tensor) 的集合. 一般的张量积空间 V ⊗ W 中的元素是这些单张量的有限线性组合. 并非所有张量都能写成单个 α ⊗ β 的形式. 7. d i m ( V ⊗ W ) = d i m V + d i m W . 判断: 假. 解析: 这是直和 V ⊕ W 的维数公式. 张量积空间的维数应为两空间维数的乘积, 即 dim ( V ⊗ W ) = dim V × dim W . 8. 若 A 是对称阵且正负惯性指数分别为 p , q , 则 tr ( A ) = p − q . 判断: 假. 解析: 矩阵的迹等于其所有特征值之和, 即 tr ( A ) = ∑ λ i ​ . 正负惯性指数 p , q 只代表正特征值和负特征值的个数, 与特征值的具体大小无关. 反例: 取 A = ( 2 0 ​ 0 − 1 ​ ) , 此时 p = 1 , q = 1 , p − q = 0 , 但 tr ( A ) = 2 − 1 = 1  = 0 . 9. 若 T 有循环向量, 则 V 除 { 0 } 与 V 之外没有其他 T 不变子空间. 判断: 假. 解析: 空间 V 没有非平凡的 T -不变子空间的充要条件是 T 的特征多项式 (或最小多项式) 在数域 F 上是不可约的. 有循环向量只能说明特征多项式等于最小多项式. 反例: 考虑 V = R 2 以及变换矩阵 T = ( 1 0 ​ 1 1 ​ ) , 它有循环向量 ( 0 , 1 ) T , 但它有一个一维的非平凡不变子空间 span {( 1 , 0 ) T } . 10. 正定实对称阵是可逆的, 且其逆也是正定实对称阵. 判断: 真. 解析: 设 A 是正定实对称阵, 则其所有特征值 λ i ​ > 0 . 因为 det ( A ) = ∏ λ i ​ > 0 , 所以 A 是可逆的. (困难) 反过来, 如果我们有 Y 是一个概形, 对 Y 的任意仿射开集 Spec B ↪ Y 指定一个理想 I ( B ) ⊂ B . 且对任意的 f ∈ B 局部化 B → B f ​ 给出了同构 I ( B ) f ​ → I ( B f ​ ) . 证明以上信息粘合成了唯一的闭子概形 X ↪ Y . 见 [ GöWe20 ] 命题 7.33. 习题 11 (有限态射) . 1. 证明有限态射是颇合的 (proper) . 2. 如果 f : X → Y 是一个仿射概形间的颇合态射, 证明 f 是有限态射. 见 [ GöWe20 ] 推论 12.89. 参考文献 [GöWe20] Ulrich Görtz, Torsten Wedhorn. 讲义：代数几何初步 · 代数簇与Hilbert零点定理 1 仿射代数簇 记域上的 n 维仿射空间 即线性空间为 k n . 在代数几何中, 我们将其记作 A n ( k ) . 以下无歧义时简记为 A n . 对于任一映射 f : A n ( k ) → k , 其零点集即 0 处的纤维 V ( f ) := { x ∈ A n ( k ) ∣ f ( x ) = 0 } . 代数几何学家感兴趣的是 f 为多项式时的情形. 定义 1.1. 称 A n 中的子集 F 为 仿射代数簇 , 若存在 k [ X 1 ​ , ⋯ , X n ​ ] 中的子集 S , 使得 F = { a ∈ A n ∣ f ( a ) = 0 , ∀ f ∈ S } . 记子集 S 对应的代数簇为 V ( S ) . 一些简单的例子或性质如下: 例 1.2. (1) V ( 1 ) = ∅ , V ( 0 ) = A n . (2) 若 S = { X 1 ​ − s 1 ​ , … , X n ​ − s n ​ } , 则 V ( S ) = {( s 1 ​ , ⋯ , s n ​ )} . 故而单点集是代数簇. (3) 若 S 1 ​ ⊂ S 2 ​ , 则 V ( S 1 ​ ) ⊃ V ( S 2 ​ ) . (4) 对于 S ⊂ A , 记 S 生成的理想为 ⟨ S ⟩ , 则 V ( S ) = V ( ⟨ S ⟩ ) . 这是由定义可验证的. 故而定义 1.1 中考虑 A 的子集与 A 的理想并无区别. 设 A 是交换幺环. 其中理想 I ⊲ A 的 根理想 定义为 I ​ := { f ∈ A ∣ 存在正整数 n 使得 f n ∈ I } . 可验证 I ​ 确实是一个理想 (这依赖于 A 的交换性) , 且 V ( I ) = V ( I ​ ) . (这是因为域是既约的) 例 1.3. 素理想都是根理想. 注 1.4. 也可以将代数簇定义为有限集 F ⊂ k [ X 1 ​ , … , X n ​ ] 的公共零点. 这则定义与定义 1.1 是等价的. 一个方向是简单的, 而另一个方向则是由 Hilbert 基定理 (若 R 是诺特环, 则 R [ X 1 ​ , … , X n ​ ] 是诺特环) , 若 I ⊲ A , 则 I 有有限生成元组 f 1 ​ , ⋯ , f n ​ , 故 V ( I ) = V ( f 1 ​ , ⋯ , f n ​ ) . 我们希望在 A n 上建立一种新的拓扑, 使得其能代替繁琐的消元等繁琐的多项式运算. 幸运的是, 这种拓扑定义起来并不麻烦. 其依赖于以下事实: 命题 1.5. 对于一族子集 { S α ​ } α ∈ I ​ ⊂ k [ X 1 ​ , … , X n ​ ] , 其中 I 为指标集, 我们有 (1) ⋂ α ​ V ( S α ​ ) = V ( ⋃ α ​ S α ​ ) . (2) V ( S 1 ​ ) ∪ V ( S 2 ​ ) = V ( S 1 ​ S 2 ​ ) . 证明. (1) “ ⊂ ”: 若 p ∈ ⋂ α ​ V ( S α ​ ) , 则对任意 f ∈ S α ​ 与 α ∈ I 有 f ( p ) = 0 , 即 p ∈ V ( ⋃ α ​ S α ​ ) . “ ⊃ ”: 若对于任意 f ∈ ⋃ α ​ S α ​ 有 f ( p ) = 0 , 则对于任意 α ∈ I 有 p ∈ V ( S α ​ ) , 即 p ∈ ⋂ α ​ V ( S α ​ ) . (2) “ ⊂ ”: 若 p ∈ V ( S 1 ​ ) ∪ V ( S 2 ​ ) , 则不妨设对于任意 f ∈ S 1 ​ , 有 f ( p ) = 0 . 那么任意 g ∈ S 1 ​ S 2 ​ , 有 g = f h , 其中 f ∈ S 1 ​ , h ∈ S 2 ​ . 那么 g ( p ) = f ( p ) h ( p ) = 0 , 即 p ∈ V ( S 1 ​ S 2 ​ ) . “ ⊃ ”: 反之, 若 p ∈ / V ( S 1 ​ ) ∪ V ( S 2 ​ ) , 则存在 f ∈ S 1 ​ 与 g ∈ S 2 ​ 使得 f ( p ) , g ( p )  = 0 , 故由整性知 f ( p ) g ( p )  = 0 . 但 f g ∈ S 1 ​ S 2 ​ , 故 p ∈ / V ( S 1 ​ S 2 ​ ) . □ 这实际上是说, A n 中的全体仿射代数簇有闭集结构. 因此, 我们可以在 A n 定义一个全新的拓扑结构, 使其中闭集恰好为全体仿射代数簇. 我们称这个拓扑为 Zariski 拓扑 . 以下无特殊说明时, A n 装备 Zariski 拓扑. 注 1.6. 注意到取 k 为 R 或 C , 则 Zariski 拓扑其实严格粗于 Euclid 拓扑. 这是由于 Euclid 拓扑下, 多项式函数都是连续函数, 但连续函数显然可以不是多项式函数. 若 n = 1 , 则 Zariski 拓扑即余有限拓扑. 而取 k 为有限域, 则 Zariski 拓扑就是离散拓扑. 值得注意的是, Zariski 拓扑不是 Hausdorff 拓扑. A n 不是 Hausdorff 空间. 这是因为 A n 中的任意两个非空开集都是相交的: 它们都形如 D ( S ) = V ( S ) c . 我们也可以定义子簇: 定义 1.7 (子簇) . 称 U 为代数簇 V 的子簇, 若 U 是 V 的闭子集. 这也等价于说 U 是代数簇且 U ⊂ V . 在代数几何中, 我们时常用到一些 R n 中不太可能出现的拓扑性质. 定义 1.8 (诺特空间) . 称拓扑空间 X 为诺特空间, 若 X 满足闭集降链条件, 即任一闭集降链 F 1 ​ ⊋ ⋯ ⊋ F n ​ ⊋ ⋯ 长度有限. (也即满足开集升链条件, 即开集升链有界.) 例 1.9. (1) 欧氏空间 R n 中的诺特子空间即有限点集与空集. (2) 仿射空间 A n 是诺特空间. 这是因为对任一闭集降链 V ( I 1 ​ ) ⊋ ⋯ ⊋ V ( I m ​ ) ⊋ ⋯ , 有 I 1 ​ ⊊ ⋯ ⊊ I m ​ ⊊ ⋯ . 而由于 A = k [ X 1 ​ , ⋯ , X n ​ ] 是诺特环, 故理想升链有界. 故而对应的闭集降链有界. (3) 诺特空间的子空间都诺特. (由子空间拓扑定义) (4) 在代数几何中, “紧” 通常称为 “拟紧”, 而 “紧” 一词指代 “拟紧且 Hausdorff”. 对于拓扑空间 X , 其诺特性等价于每一个子空间都拟紧. (见 Atiyah 习题 6.6.) 另一个代数几何中的特有拓扑概念是 “不可约” 性. 定义 1.10 (不可约空间) . 称拓扑空间 X 不可约, 若它不能写为两个真闭子集的并. 这也等价于任意非空开子集稠密. 称 X 的子集不可约, 若该子集作为子空间不可约. 注 1.11. 1. 在欧氏空间中, 不可约子集只有单点集与空集. 2. 取 k = C , 则仿射直线 A C 1 ​ 不可约. (只需注意到这时的 Zariski 拓扑是余有限拓扑.) 3. 连续映射正向保持不可约性. 4. 子集 V 为不可约集 当且仅当 V 为不可约集. 5. 不可约空间是连通的. 我们将会看到, 不可约集是一个很好处理的对象. 下述定理保证了不可约集在诺特空间中具有某种一般性. 定理 1.12 (不可约分解) . 对于诺特空间 X , 存在 有限 个不可约闭子集 Y i ​ ⊂ X 使得 (1) X = ⋃ i = 1 n ​ Y i ​ ; (2) 且对于任意 i  = j 有 Y i ​  ⊂ Y j ​ . 且这样的分解在差一个 { Y i ​ } 的重排的意义下是 唯一 的. 证明. 存在性 : 先证明满足条件 (1) 的分解存在. 不妨设 X 可约, 否则 X = X 即为这样的分解. 若 X 不满足这样的性质 (即不能写为有限个不可约闭子集的并) , 令 X = X 1 ​ ∪ Y 1 ​ , 其中 X 1 ​ , Y 1 ​ 是 X 的真闭子集. 由假设, 不妨设 X 1 ​ 可约, 则可分解为 X 1 ​ = X 2 ​ ∪ Y 2 ​ , 其中 X 2 ​ , Y 2 ​ 是 X 1 ​ 的真闭子集, 故自动是 X 的真闭子集 (由于可写为两个闭集的交) . 由假设, 不妨设 X i ​ 可约, 则继续操作得真闭子集 X i + 1 ​ . 如此得一闭子集降链 X ⊃ X 1 ​ ⊃ ⋯ ⊃ X i ​ ⊃ ⋯ 与诺特性矛盾. 唯一性 : 若 Y = ⋃ i = 1 n ​ Y i ​ = ⋃ j = 1 m ​ Z j ​ 是满足条件 (1) 与 (2) 的分解, 则 Z j ​ = Z j ​ ∩ Y = ⋃ i = 1 n ​ ( Z j ​ ∩ Y i ​ ) . 由 Z j ​ 的不可约性及条件 (2), 存在唯一 σ ( j ) 使得 Z j ​ = Y σ ( j ) ​ ∩ Z j ​ , 即 Z j ​ ⊃ Y σ ( j ) ​ . 同理, 存在 τ ( σ ( j )) 使得 Z τ ( σ ( j )) ​ ⊂ Y σ ( j ) ​ ⊂ Z j ​ . 由条件 (2) 知 τ ( σ ( j )) = j , 且 Z j ​ = Y σ ( j ) ​ . 那么 σ : { 1 , ⋯ , m } → { 1 , ⋯ , n } 与 τ : { 1 , ⋯ , n } → { 1 , ⋯ , m } 是互逆的映射, 从而 τ 是双射, 且 n = m . 故 { Z j ​ } 实则是 { Y i ​ } 的一个重排. □ 注 1.13. 不可约分解不一定是无交并. 例如 V ( X Y ) ⊂ A 2 的不可约分解为 V ( X Y ) = V ( X ) ∪ V ( Y ) , 两个不可约分支有交点 ( 0 , 0 ) . 但当 V 是代数群时, 不可约分解确实是无交并. 上述定理用在 A n 上即: 推论 1.14. 若 V 是一个仿射代数簇, 则存在有限个互不包含的不可约子簇 { V i ​ } i = 1 n ​ , 使得 V = ⋃ i = 1 n ​ V i ​ . 且这样的分解是唯一的. 进而许多关于代数簇的命题将得以化归到仿射代数簇上讨论. 讲义：代数几何初步 · 维数理论 1 簇与环的 Krull 维数 定义 1.1 (拓扑空间的 Kurll 维数) . 若 X 是一个拓扑空间, 则定义 X 的维数为不可约闭集升链的最大长度, 即 dim Krull ​ X := sup { n ∣ F 0 ​ ⊊ F 1 ​ ⊊ ⋯ ⊊ F n ​ , F i ​ 不可约闭 } . 以下简记 dim X . 这实际上是与我们的一般认知兼容的. 下文会证明 dim A n = n . 这与其作为线性空间的维数一致. 命题 1.2. 我们整理一些 Krull 维数的基本刻画: (1) 若 Y ⊂ X , 则 dim Y ≤ dim X . (2) 若 Y ⊊ X 且 dim X < ∞ , 且 X 不可约, Y 闭, 则 dim Y < dim X . (3) 若 { X i ​ } i = 1 n ​ 是 X 的开覆盖, 则 dim X = 1 ≤ i ≤ n max ​ { dim X i ​ } . 证明. (1) 若 Y 0 ​ ⊊ Y 1 ​ ⊊ ⋯ ⊊ Y n ​ 是 Y 中不可约闭集升链, 则 Y 0 ​ ​ ⊊ Y 1 ​ ​ ⊊ ⋯ ⊊ Y n ​ ​ 是 X 中不可约闭集升链. 因而 dim Y ≤ dim X . (2) 若 Y 0 ​ ⊊ Y 1 ​ ⊊ ⋯ ⊊ Y n ​ 是 Y 中不可约闭集升链, 则 Y 0 ​ ⊊ Y 1 ​ ⊊ ⋯ ⊊ Y n ​ ⊂ X 是 X 中的不可约闭集升链. 因而 dim Y < dim X . (3) 显然 dim X ≥ 1 ≤ i ≤ n max ​ { dim X i ​ } . 若 Y 0 ​ ⊊ Y 1 ​ ⊊ ⋯ ⊊ Y n ​ 是 X 中不可约闭集升链, 则存在 X j ​ 使得 X j ​ ∩ Y 0 ​  = ∅ . 故 X j ​ ∩ Y 0 ​ 是 Y 0 ​ 的开子集, 故不可约. 而 X j ​ ∩ Y 0 ​ 是 X j ​ 的闭子集, 故 X j ​ ∩ Y 0 ​ ⊂ X j ​ ∩ Y 1 ​ ⊂ ⋯ ⊂ X j ​ ∩ Y n ​ 是 X j ​ 中的闭子集升链. 该升链事实上是严格的, 因为 Y i ​ ∩ X j ​ 在 Y i ​ 中的闭包即 X 中的闭包 (由于 Y i ​ 闭) . 且由不可约性, Y i ​ ∩ X j ​ ​ = Y i ​ . 这说明了 dim X ≤ dim X j ​ . 这证明了反向的不等式. □ 命题 1.3. 若 X 是零维簇, 则 ∣ X ∣ < ∞ . 证明. 令 X = ⋃ i = 1 n ​ X i ​ 为不可约分解, 则 dim X i ​ = 0 . 若 X i ​ 不是单点集, 则取 p ∈ X , 则 p 是 X i ​ 的真闭子集, 故而 dim X < 0 , 矛盾! 故而 ∣ X i ​ ∣ = 1 , 进而 ∣ X ∣ = n < ∞ . □ 定义 1.4 (等维数空间 (Space of Pure Dimension) ) . 称 X 是等维数的, 若其不可约分支具有相等的维数. 例 1.5. 如 V ( X Y ) = V ( X ) ∪ V ( Y ) . 定义 1.6 (局部维数 (Local Dimension) ) . 对于拓扑空间 X , 我们可以定义 p ∈ X 处的局部维数为 dim p ​ X := sup { n ∣ p ⊊ F 1 ​ ⊊ ⋯ ⊊ F n ​ , F i ​ 不可约闭 } . 注 1.7. 局部维数显然不高于拓扑空间的维数. (注: 这里不使用 “整体维数” 一词, 因为其在同调代数中另有所指.) 我们也可以定义环的 Krull 维数. 定义 1.8 (交换幺环的 Krull 维数) . 定义 dim Krull ​ R = sup { n ∣ p 0 ​ ⊊ p 1 ​ ⊊ ⋯ ⊊ p n ​ , p i ​ ∈ Spec R } . (2) 椭圆曲线. 详情参见相关条目, 这是一个非线性代数群. 在 k = C 的情形下, 线性代数群已被完全分类. 定义 4.4 (Abel 簇 (Abelian Variety) ) . 称不可约的射影代数群为 Abel 簇. (即作为簇是射影簇的代数群) 定理 4.5. Abel 簇都是交换代数群. 证明. 令 X 是 Abel 簇, 定义 u : X × X → X ; ( x , y ) ↦ x − 1 y − 1 x y . 注意到 u ( X × e ) = e , 故由上述命题知 u ( X × { y }) 都是单点集. 但 u ( e × { y }) = e , 故这意味着 x − 1 y − 1 x y = 1 对于任意 x , y ∈ X 成立. 这即 X 交换. □ 一维的复 Abel 簇就是椭圆曲线, 故上述命题证明椭圆曲线上的群结构是交换的. 5 可构造集 定义 5.1 (可构造集 (Constructible Set) ) . 称拓扑空间 X 的子集 Y 是可构造的, 若 Y 是有限个相对闭集的并. 这也即 Y = ⋃ i = 1 n ​ U i ​ ∩ V i ​ , 其中 U i ​ 开而 V i ​ 闭. 注 5.2. 开闭集显然都是可构造集. 定理 5.3 (Chevalley) . 若 φ : X → Y 是簇的态射, 则 φ 保持可构造集. 作为推论, 簇的像是可构造的. 证明. 由于可构造集对有限并封闭, 故不妨设 X 不可约. 由于 X 的相对闭集也是簇, 故只需证 φ ( X ) 可构造. 若 φ 不是支配态射, 则将 Y 缩小至 φ ( X ) ​ . 对 dim Y = 0 , 命题显然成立. 若命题对维数小于 dim φ ( X ) 成立. 由上述内容知, 存在开集 V ⊂ Y 使得对于任意 y ∈ V 有 dim φ − 1 ( y ) = dim X − dim Y . 令 Z = φ − 1 ( V ) c , 则由不可约性有 φ ( X ) = φ ( Z ) ∪ U . 那么由归纳假设, φ ( Z ) 是可构造的, 故而 φ ( X ) 可构造. 故归纳假设成立, 命题得证. □ 例 5.4. Chevalley 定理证明了代数群的像都是闭子群. 这是因为代数子群的闭性等价于可构造性. 而若 φ : G 1 ​ → G 2 ​ 是代数群的态射, 那么 φ ( G 1 ​ ) 依 Chevalley 定理是可构造的, 故而在 G 2 ​ 中闭.

讲义：模空间与代数叠 · Grothendieck拓扑与层 1 从拓扑到景 Grothendieck 拓扑与景 我们先回顾拓扑空间上的层论. 记 Top ( X ) 为拓扑空间 X 上的全体开集构成的范畴: 其中的对象为 X 的开子集, 而态射为开集的嵌入. 给定范畴 C , 拓扑空间上的一个 预层 指的是一个反变函子 F : Top ( X ) op → C . 这是说对于每个开集 U ⊆ X , 我们指定一个 C 中的对象; 而对于每一组开集的包含 i : V ↪ U , 在 C 中有 限制态射 F ( i ) : F ( U ) → F ( V ) . 且对于同构 U ≅ ​ U , 其限制态射是恒等. 而一个预层 F 成为 层 的条件是如下粘结公理: 对于任何开覆盖 { U i ​ } i ∈ I ​ (记嵌入 σ i ​ : U i ​ → U ) F ( U ) ∏ i ∈ I ​ F ( σ i ​ ) ​ ∏ i ​ F ( U i ​ ) ∏ i , j ​ F ( U i ​ ∩ U j ​ ) ∏ i , j ∈ I ​ F ( π i , j 1 ​ ) ∏ i , j ∈ I ​ F ( π i , j 2 ​ ) 是等化子图表, 其中 π i , j 1 ​ : U i ​ ∩ U j ​ → U i ​ , π i , j 2 ​ : U i ​ ∩ U j ​ → U j ​ . 注意到 U i ​ ∩ U j ​ = U i ​ × U ​ U j ​ . 这个事实引导我们在一般的范畴上做拓扑时, 对于 “开集” 来说, 做交的正确对应是做纤维积. 另外, 从上面我们看到, 判定预层是否为层时, 真正重要的并不是开集本身, 而是开覆盖. 这些事实给了我们将 “拓扑” 推广到别的范畴上的范式: 定义 1.1. 范畴 C 上的一个 Grothendieck 拓扑 是指满足如下条件的映射 Cov : Ob ( C ) → 2 Mor ( C ) : (1) 对于每个对象 X ∈ C , X 的 覆盖 Cov ( X ) 是幂集 2 { U → X : Y ∈ C } 的子集; (2) ( 平凡覆盖 ) 若有同构 U ≅ ​ X , 则 { U ≅ ​ X } ∈ Cov ( X ) ; (3) ( 加细 ) 若 { U i ​ → X } i ∈ I ​ ∈ Cov ( X ) , 且 { V ij ​ → U i ​ } j ∈ J i ​ ​ ∈ Cov ( U i ​ ) , 那么 { V ij ​ → U i ​ → X } i ∈ I , j ∈ J i ​ ​ ∈ Cov ( X ) ; (4) ( 基变换 ) 若 { U i ​ → X } i ∈ I ​ , 且有箭头 Y → X , 那么诸纤维积 Y × X ​ U i ​ 存在, 且 { Y × X ​ U i ​ → Y } i ∈ I ​ ∈ Cov ( Y ) . 定义 1.2. 一个 景 是指一个范畴 C 与其上的一个 Grothendieck 拓扑 Cov 构成的二元数据 ( C , Cov ) . 例 1.3. 我们尝试将古典的 Zariski 拓扑兼并入 Grothendieck 拓扑的框架下. 对于概形 S , 考虑俯范畴 Sch S ​ . 定义 S Zar ​ 为 ( Sch S ​ , Cov ) , 其中 Cov 定义为 Cov ([ X → S ]) = { S − 开浸入族 { σ i ​ : U i ​ → X }} ，且 i ⋃ ​ ∣ σ ( U i ​ ) ∣ = X } . 该景称为 大 Zariski 景 . 这其实是将开子集这一概念同开浸入等同起来的结果. 几类态射的性质 定义 1.4. 一个概形态射 X → Y 如果是 局部有限展示 的 忠实平坦 态射, 则称其是 fppf 的. 2 景上之层 预层、层与层化 例子 3 代数空间 定义 3.1. 对于概形 S 与俯范畴 Sch S ​ 上的一种 Grothendieck 拓扑 τ , S -空间 是指 ( Sch S ​ ) τ ​ 上的一个层. S -空间的态射即层的态射. 例 3.2 (概形视作层) . 定义 3.3. 对于概形 S , 其上的 代数空间 X 指的是 ( Sch S ​ ) e ˊ t ​ 上满足如下两个条件的层: (1) 对于任意两个概形 X , Y 以及 S -空间态射 s : X → X 与 y : Y → X , 层 X × X ​ Y 可被概形表出; (2) 存在一个概形 U 以及一个平展满射 p : U t o X , 即对于任何概形 Y , U × X ​ Y → Y 是概形间的平展满射. 该态射 P : U → X 成为 坐标卡 .

讲义：模空间与代数叠 · 模函子及其可表性 1 模空间问题简介 “分类” 空间 代数几何的终极问题之一是分类代数簇. 这个问题派生出了许多不同的学问. 比如双有理几何的目的是为了在双有理等价的意义下分类代数簇. 另一种办法是对具有共性的一类目标进行参数化. 思考如下例子: 例 1.1. 考虑 P 2 ( C ) 中的二次曲线. 若坐标为 x , y , z , 那么任一二次曲线都形如 a x 2 + b y 2 + c z 2 + d x y + e x z + f yz = 0. 由于每个这样的方程定义相同的二次曲线当且仅当其系数差一个共同的倍数, 我们发现平面二次曲线与 P 5 ( C ) 中的点是一一对应的. 某种意义上, 我们可以说 P 5 是平面二次曲线的分类空间. 这则例子在后续 Hilbert 概形的章节会被严格化. 在这则例子中, 我们将每条代数曲线都对应到了 P C 5 ​ 中的闭点上去. 换而言之, 我们找到了一个几何对象, 使其中的每个点参数化我们给定的一族对象. 在代数拓扑中有一个类似的办法来分类一种特殊的几何对象——向量丛. 对于任一个群 G , 存在一个空间 B G 与其上的 G -主丛 E G → B G , 满足对于任何与一个流形 M , M 到 B G 的映射同伦类 [ M , B G ] 与 M 上的 G 主丛一一对应. 这个一一对应由 E G 的拉回实现. 我们称 B G 为 分类空间 , 而 E G 为 万有线丛 . 一则典型应用如下: 实向量丛正好是 GL n ​ ( R ) -主丛, 而类似地, 复向量丛可看作 GL n ​ ( C ) . 所以流形 M 上的实向量丛全体同伦类正好是 [ M , BGL n ​ ( R )] , 而复向量丛全体的同伦类则是 [ M , BGL n ​ ( C )] . BGL n ​ ( R ) 有一个十分好的刻画, 即无穷维 Grassman 流形 G n ​ ( R ∞ ) . 其 Γ 系数的上同调的生成元是已知的 (其中 Γ 是含 2 1 ​ 的整环) . 这些生成元在对应的 M → BGL n ​ ( R ) 下给出 Potryagin 类 (在偶数维时还会给出欧拉类) . 而复的版本给出陈类. 这则思路下, 流形上的 G -主丛的同伦类全体被实现为流形到某个具体空间映射的同伦类. 在代数几何中, 这就是模空间的雏形. 模函子的定义范畴也通常是 Sch 的俯范畴 Sch S ​ . 注意到 Sch = Sch Z ​ . 可表性问题及其解决办法 定义 1.2. 对于模函子 h : Sch o p → Sets , 若概形 M 使 h ≅ h M ​ , 则称 M 为 h 的 细模空间 . 注意到一旦 M 存在, 由米田引理知它是同构意义下唯一的. 细模空间是对一个模问题的最好答案: 如果模函子 h 被 M 表出, 那么这就可以保留这个模问题的所有信息. 这其中也包括给出任何一族我们想要的对象的刻画. 具体来说, 存在 万有族 U → M 使得对于任意一族考虑的对象 X → S , 都存在一个态射 f : S → M 使得 T ≅ U × M , f ​ S . 但细模空间对于许多模问题来说都是不存在的. 这其中包括一些研究的比较透彻的例子, 例如曲线、K3 曲面、Abel 簇、Enrique 曲面的模空间、向量丛的模空间等. 在概形的框架下, 一则解决办法是 粗模空间 . 定义 1.3. 对于模函子 h : Sch o p → Sets , 若存在概形 M 与函子 Φ : h → h M ​ 使 (a) 对于任何域 k , Φ ( Spec ( k )) : h ( Spec ( k )) → h M ​ ( Spec ( k )) 是双射; 讲义：相交理论 · Hodge Index Theorem 定理 0.1. Suppose X is an irreducible smooth projective surface over a field k . Let L , H ∈ Pic ( X ) be line bundles such that H ⋅ H > 0 and L ⋅ H = 0 . Then: (a) L ⋅ L ≤ 0 . (b) L ⋅ L = 0 if and only if L ≡ num ​ 0 . Proof. The proof proceeds in several steps. Step 1: 引理 0.2. If H is an ample line bundle and M is a line bundle such that ( M ⋅ H ) > ( ω X ​ ⋅ H ) , then h 2 ( X , M ) = 0 . Proof of Lemma 1. By Serre duality, we have h 2 ( X , M ) = h 0 ( X , ω X ​ ⊗ M ∨ ) . We prove this by contradiction. Suppose that h 0 ( X , ω X ​ ⊗ M ∨ )  = 0 . Then there exists an effective divisor D such that O ( D ) ≅ ω X ​ ⊗ M ∨ . By the ampleness of H and the effectiveness of D , we must have ( H ⋅ D ) > 0 . On the other hand, since D ≡ ω X ​ − M , this implies ( ω X ​ ⋅ H ) > ( M ⋅ H ) . This directly contradicts our initial assumption! Thus, h 2 ( X , M ) = 0 . □ Step 2: 引理 0.3. If H is an ample line bundle, and L is a line bundle with L ⋅ L > 0 and L ⋅ H > 0 , then for n ≫ 0 , the tensor power L ⊗ n has a non-zero global section (i.e., h 0 ( X , L ⊗ n ) > 0 ). Proof of Lemma 2. Since L ⋅ H > 0 , we can find a sufficiently large integer n ≫ 0 such that n ( L ⋅ H ) > ( ω X ​ ⋅ H ) . By Lemma 1, this implies h 2 ( X , L ⊗ n ) = 0 . Applying the Riemann-Roch theorem for surfaces to L ⊗ n , we obtain: h 0 ( X , L ⊗ n ) − h 1 ( X , L ⊗ n ) ​ = χ ( X , L ⊗ n ) = 2 n 2 ​ ( L ⋅ L ) − 2 n ​ ( L ⋅ ω X ​ ) + χ ( X , O X ​ ) . ​ Since L ⋅ L > 0 , the quadratic term 2 n 2 ​ ( L ⋅ L ) strictly dominates the expression for large n . Therefore, for n ≫ 0 , the right-hand side approaches infinity, which implies h 0 ( X , L ⊗ n ) − h 1 ( X , L ⊗ n ) > 0 . Since h 1 ( X , L ⊗ n ) ≥ 0 , it immediately follows that h 0 ( X , L ⊗ n ) > 0 . □ Step 3: We now prove the main theorem for the specific case where H is ample. For n ≫ 0 , the line bundle L ⊗ H ⊗ n becomes ample (or very ample). Let us denote this ample line bundle by H ′ . We proceed to prove the theorem by contradiction. Suppose that L ⋅ L > 0 . Compute the intersection: ( L ⋅ H ′ ) = ( L ⋅ ( L ⊗ H ⊗ n )) = ( L ⋅ L ) + n ( L ⋅ H ) = ( L ⋅ L ) > 0. By Lemma 2, since H ′ is ample, ( L ⋅ L ) > 0 , and ( L ⋅ H ′ ) > 0 , the line bundle L ⊗ m must have a non-zero global section for some integer m ≫ 0 . Let D ∈ ∣ L ⊗ m ∣ be the corresponding effective divisor. Since H is ample, its intersection with any effective divisor is strictly positive, hence ( D ⋅ H ) > 0 . This implies m 1 ​ ( D ⋅ H ) = ( L ⋅ H ) > 0 . This directly contradicts our initial assumption that ( L ⋅ H ) = 0 ! Therefore, we must have ( L ⋅ L ) ≤ 0 . Step 4: The case ( L ⋅ L ) = 0 when H is ample. Suppose ( L ⋅ L ) = 0 . We wish to prove that L ≡ num ​ 0 . We proceed by contradiction and suppose L  ≡ num ​ 0 . By definition, there exists a line bundle Q such that ( Q ⋅ L )  = 0 . Consider the line bundle (written additively): R := ( H ⋅ H ) Q − ( Q ⋅ H ) H . We can verify the following intersections: ( R ⋅ H ) = ( H ⋅ H ) ( Q ⋅ H ) − ( Q ⋅ H ) ( H ⋅ H ) = 0. ( R ⋅ L ) = ( H ⋅ H ) ( Q ⋅ L ) − ( Q ⋅ H ) ( H ⋅ L ) = ( H ⋅ H ) ( Q ⋅ L )  = 0. Now, define L ′ := R ⊗ L ⊗ m (additively R + m L ). We have: ( L ′ ⋅ H ) = ( R ⋅ H ) + m ( L ⋅ H ) = 0 + 0 = 0. By the conclusion of Step 3, since ( L ′ ⋅ H ) = 0 , it must follow that ( L ′ ⋅ L ′ ) ≤ 0 . However, let us compute ( L ′ ⋅ L ′ ) directly: ( L ′ ⋅ L ′ ) = ( R ⋅ R ) + 2 m ( R ⋅ L ) + m 2 ( L ⋅ L ) = ( R ⋅ R ) + 2 m ( R ⋅ L ) . Because ( R ⋅ L )  = 0 , the term 2 m ( R ⋅ L ) is a non-constant linear function of m . We can choose some integer m ∈ Z such that ( R ⋅ R ) + 2 m ( R ⋅ L ) > 0 . This yields ( L ′ ⋅ L ′ ) > 0 , which contradicts the conclusion ( L ′ ⋅ L ′ ) ≤ 0 . Therefore, L ≡ num ​ 0 . This completes the proof of the Hodge Index Theorem for the case where H is ample. Step 5: The general case. Now suppose H is not necessarily ample, but only satisfies ( H ⋅ H ) > 0 . Let A be an arbitrary ample line bundle on X . If ( A ⋅ L ) = 0 , then by applying the established ample case to A , we immediately get ( L ⋅ L ) ≤ 0 (and ( L ⋅ L ) = 0 if and only if L ≡ num ​ 0 ). The theorem holds. If ( A ⋅ L )  = 0 , then trivially L  ≡ num ​ 0 . Also, note that if ( A ⋅ H ) = 0 , applying the ample case to A would yield ( H ⋅ H ) ≤ 0 , which contradicts the given condition ( H ⋅ H ) > 0 . Thus, we must have ( A ⋅ H )  = 0 . Consider the line bundle: M := ( A ⋅ L ) H − ( A ⋅ H ) L . Intersecting with A , we get: ( A ⋅ M ) = ( A ⋅ L ) ( A ⋅ H ) − ( A ⋅ H ) ( A ⋅ L ) = 0. Since A is ample and ( A ⋅ M ) = 0 , we can apply the ample case to deduce that ( M ⋅ M ) ≤ 0 . Let us expand ( M ⋅ M ) using the bilinearity of the intersection form: ( M ⋅ M ) = ( A ⋅ L ) 2 ( H ⋅ H ) − 2 ( A ⋅ L ) ( A ⋅ H ) ( H ⋅ L ) + ( A ⋅ H ) 2 ( L ⋅ L ) ≤ 0. Since ( L ⋅ H ) = 0 by assumption, the middle cross-term vanishes, leaving: > 0 ( A ⋅ L ) 2 ​ ​ > 0 ( H ⋅ H ) ​ ​ + > 0 ( A ⋅ H ) 2 ​ ​ ( L ⋅ L ) ≤ 0. The first term is strictly positive because ( A ⋅ L )  = 0 and ( H ⋅ H ) > 0 . The coefficient ( A ⋅ H ) 2 is also strictly positive. For the entire sum to be non-positive, we must necessarily have: ( L ⋅ L ) < 0. This concludes the proof of the Hodge Index Theorem for the general case. □ We introduce the following interesting consequence: 引理 0.4 (Neron–Severi group) . N 1 ​ ( X ) := Div ( X ) / ∼ , where ∼ is the numerical equivalence relation. Then N 1 ​ ( X ) is a free abelian group of finite rank. 推论 0.5. Let X be an irreducible smooth projective surface over a field k . Let ρ be the Picard number of X . (a) In the rational Néron-Severi space N 1 ( X ) Q ​ = ( Pic ( X ) / ≡ num ​ ) ⊗ Q , there exists an orthogonal basis e 1 ​ , e 2 ​ , … , e ρ ​ such that the intersection form is diagonal with exactly one strictly positive entry and ρ − 1 strictly negative entries. (b) In the real Néron-Severi space N 1 ( X ) R ​ = N 1 ( X ) Q ​ ⊗ Q ​ R , there exists an orthogonal basis u 1 ​ , u 2 ​ , … , u ρ ​ such that the intersection matrix is exactly diag ( 1 , − 1 , … , − 1 ) . Proof. Proof of (a): The N 1 ( X ) Q ​ case. Since X is a projective surface, there exists an ample line bundle H . Let e 1 ​ = [ H ] ∈ N 1 ( X ) Q ​ be its numerical class. Because H is ample, its self-intersection is strictly positive, meaning e 1 ​ ⋅ e 1 ​ > 0 . We define the orthogonal complement of e 1 ​ in N 1 ( X ) Q ​ with respect to the intersection form: e 1 ⊥ ​ = { D ∈ N 1 ( X ) Q ​ ∣ D ⋅ e 1 ​ = 0 } . Because e 1 ​ ⋅ e 1 ​  = 0 , the intersection form is non-degenerate along the one-dimensional subspace spanned by e 1 ​ . Therefore, we have an orthogonal direct sum decomposition of the ρ -dimensional vector space N 1 ( X ) Q ​ : N 1 ( X ) Q ​ = Q e 1 ​ ⊕ e 1 ⊥ ​ . The dimension of e 1 ⊥ ​ is exactly ρ − 1 . By the Hodge Index Theorem, for any non-zero element L ∈ e 1 ⊥ ​ , we have L ⋅ e 1 ​ = 0 and L  ≡ num ​ 0 . The theorem guarantees that L ⋅ L < 0 . This implies that the restriction of the intersection form to the subspace e 1 ⊥ ​ is strictly negative definite. Since every definite symmetric bilinear form over a field of characteristic zero admits an orthogonal basis (via the Gram-Schmidt orthogonalization process), there exists an orthogonal basis e 2 ​ , … , e ρ ​ for e 1 ⊥ ​ . Therefore, { e 1 ​ , e 2 ​ , … , e ρ ​ } forms an orthogonal basis for the entire space N 1 ( X ) Q ​ . Under this basis, the intersection matrix is diagonal. The diagonal entries are e 1 ​ ⋅ e 1 ​ > 0 and e i ​ ⋅ e i ​ < 0 for i = 2 , … , ρ . Thus, the signature of the intersection form is ( + , − , … , − ) . Proof of (b): The N 1 ( X ) R ​ case. We now extend the scalars to the real numbers, considering the space N 1 ( X ) R ​ . The orthogonal basis { e 1 ​ , e 2 ​ , … , e ρ ​ } found in part (a) naturally serves as an orthogonal basis for N 1 ( X ) R ​ . Over the real numbers, we can normalize these basis vectors because every positive real number has a well-defined real square root. We define a new basis { u 1 ​ , u 2 ​ , … , u ρ ​ } by scaling the previous basis vectors: u 1 ​ = e 1 ​ ⋅ e 1 ​ ​ 1 ​ e 1 ​ , and for i = 2 , … , ρ , u i ​ = − ( e i ​ ⋅ e i ​ ) ​ 1 ​ e i ​ . We can compute the self-intersections of this new basis. For u 1 ​ , we have: u 1 ​ ⋅ u 1 ​ = ( e 1 ​ ⋅ e 1 ​ ​ 1 ​ ) 2 ( e 1 ​ ⋅ e 1 ​ ) = e 1 ​ ⋅ e 1 ​ e 1 ​ ⋅ e 1 ​ ​ = 1. For i ≥ 2 , since e i ​ ⋅ e i ​ < 0 , the quantity − ( e i ​ ⋅ e i ​ ) is strictly positive, so its real square root is well-defined. We have: u i ​ ⋅ u i ​ = ( − ( e i ​ ⋅ e i ​ ) ​ 1 ​ ) 2 ( e i ​ ⋅ e i ​ ) = − ( e i ​ ⋅ e i ​ ) e i ​ ⋅ e i ​ ​ = − 1. Since scaling vectors does not affect their mutual orthogonality, { u 1 ​ , … , u ρ ​ } is an orthogonal basis for N 1 ( X ) R ​ . Under this normalized basis, the intersection matrix is exactly the diagonal matrix diag ( 1 , − 1 , … , − 1 ) . □

Let L 1 ​ , … , L n ​ be line bundles on X . Then the intersection number is defined as: ( L 1 ​ … L n ​ ⋅ F ) := { i 1 ​ , … , i m ​ } ⊆ { 1 , … , n } ∑ ​ ( − 1 ) m χ ( X , L i 1 ​ ∨ ​ ⊗ ⋯ ⊗ L i m ​ ∨ ​ ⊗ F ) 定义 0.2 (Notations) . By this proposition, we can always assume the base field k is infinite when proving properties of the intersection number. 命题 0.6 (20.1.C) . (a) Let X be a projective curve and L be a line bundle on X . Then ( L ⋅ X ) = de g L . (This holds because ( L ⋅ X ) = − χ ( L ∨ ) + χ ( O X ​ ) = − de g L ∨ = de g L by 18.4.M.) Consider the short exact sequence: 0 → L n ∨ ​ ∣ Y ​ → O Y ​ → O Y ∩ H n ​ ​ → 0. Tensoring this sequence with ( ⨂ j  = n ​ L j ∨ ​ ) ∣ ∣ ​ Y ​ and utilizing the additive property of the Euler characteristic, we obtain: ( L 1 ​ … L n ​ ⋅ Y ) ​ = n ∈ / { i 1 ​ , … , i m ​ } ∑ ​ ( − 1 ) m ( χ ( L i 1 ​ ∨ ​ ∣ Y ​ ⊗ ⋯ ⊗ L i m ​ ∨ ​ ∣ Y ​ ) − χ ( L i 1 ​ ∨ ​ ∣ Y ​ ⊗ ⋯ ⊗ L i m ​ ∨ ​ ∣ Y ​ ⊗ L n ∨ ​ ∣ Y ​ ) ) = n ∈ / { i 1 ​ , … , i m ​ } ∑ ​ ( − 1 ) m χ ( L i 1 ​ ∨ ​ ∣ Y ​ ⊗ ⋯ ⊗ L i m ​ ∨ ​ ∣ Y ​ ⊗ O Y ∩ H n ​ ​ ) = ( L 1 ​ … L n − 1 ​ ⋅ Y ∩ H n ​ ) . ​ Applying this reduction repeatedly, we eventually conclude that: ( L 1 ​ … L n ​ ⋅ Y ) = ( O ⋅ Y ∩ H 1 ​ ⋯ ∩ H n ​ ) = de g ( Y ∩ H 1 ​ ⋯ ∩ H n ​ ) = d 1 ​ … d n ​ de g Y . □ We can get one technical consequence from the above proof: 命题 0.7 (20.1.D) . Let D be an effective Cartier divisor on X , and let Y ↪ X be a closed subscheme such that D ∣ Y ​ = D ∩ Y . Then: ( L 1 ​ … L n − 1 ​ ⋅ O ( D ) ⋅ Y ) = ( L 1 ​ … L n − 1 ​ ⋅ D ∣ Y ​ ) . 定义 0.8 (Notation) . If L i ​ = O ( D i ​ ) , we often denote the intersection number simply by using the divisors: ( L 1 ​ … L n ​ ⋅ F ) = ( D 1 ​ … D n ​ ⋅ F ) . 命题 0.9 (20.1.3) . Let X be a projective k -variety and fix a coherent sheaf F . Then the intersection number ( L 1 ​ … L n ​ ⋅ F ) is a symmetric multilinear function of the line bundles L 1 ​ , … , L n ​ . 注 0.10. The previous properties held without needing the assumption that dim ( Supp F ) ≤ n . However, starting with this multilinearity property, that dimension condition becomes essential. 注 0.11. Recall that L 1 ​ ⊗ L 2 ​ = O ( D 1 ​ ) ⊗ O ( D 2 ​ ) = O ( D 1 ​ + D 2 ​ ) . Because of this, we can write the tensor product additively as L 1 ​ + L 2 ​ . The “addition” referred to in the multilinearity of the intersection number corresponds to this tensor product of line bundles. Proof of 20.1.3. The symmetry of the intersection number is clear directly from the definition. Furthermore, by the base change property (20.1.B) 0.4 , we may assume without loss of generality that the base field k is infinite. We will prove the multilinearity by induction on n . Now we handle the base case for n = 1 ( 20.1.E ). We have following observation : Let A be a very ample line bundle on X . This gives a closed immersion X ↪ P into a projective space P such that the pullback of O ( 1 ) is exactly A . We can choose a hyperplane H of P such that the dimension of Supp ( F ) ∩ H drops by one, or dim ( Supp ( F ) ∩ H ) = 0 (meaning it consists of a finite number of points). Consider the standard short exact sequence: 0 → A ∨ → O X ​ → O X ∩ H ​ → 0. I claim that we can choose a hyperplane H as above such that tensoring this sequence with F (i.e., applying the functor − ⊗ F ) remains, in fact, exact. Supplement to the previous claim: We only need the hyperplane H to avoid the associated primes Ass ( F ) of F . This is achievable because the set of associated primes is finite ( ∣ Ass ( F ) ∣ < ∞ ). Therefore, Pic ( X ) can be generated by the classes of l and e , and their intersection numbers are as stated. Finally, from the intersection numbers, we can verify that l and e are linearly independent in Pic ( X ) , confirming that Pic ( X ) = Z l ⊕ Z e . □ Motivated by the above discussion, we have the following definition: 定义 0.11 (20.2.8) . Let X be a surface over a field k . Let C ⊆ X be a curve consisting of smooth points such that C ≅ P k 1 ​ and its self-intersection number is ( C ⋅ C ) = − 1 . We call such a curve C a ( − 1 ) -curve. A glimpse: X is a smooth projective surface over C . It is called minimal if it does not contain any rational (i.e. birational to P C 1 ​ ) ( − 1 ) -curves. There is a conclusion that if ∣ m K X ​ ∣  = 0 for some m > 0 , then X is minimal if and only if K X ​ is nef, i.e. ( K X ​ ⋅ C ) ≥ 0 for every curve C ⊆ X . 注 0.12. By analyzing the generators of Pic ( P 1 × P 1 ) and Pic ( Bl p ​ P 2 ) along with their intersection forms, we can deduce that P 1 × P 1  ≅ Bl p ​ P 2 . Classical Example (20.2.G): Note that l ≅ P 1 ≅ e . Let us take two copies of Bl p ​ P 2 , denoted as Y 1 ​ and Y 2 ​ . In Y 1 ​ , we have the naturally embedded curves l 1 ​ and e 1 ​ ; in Y 2 ​ , we have the curves l 2 ​ and e 2 ​ . We construct a new space X by gluing Y 1 ​ and Y 2 ​ along these curves such that l 1 ​ is identified with e 2 ​ , and e 1 ​ is identified with l 2 ​ . Suppose, for the sake of contradiction, that X is a projective scheme. Then there exists an ample line bundle L on X . Let L 1 ​ and L 2 ​ be the pullbacks of L via the natural inclusions Y 1 ​ ↪ X and Y 2 ​ ↪ X , respectively. Since the restriction of an ample line bundle to a closed subscheme remains ample, both L 1 ​ and L 2 ​ must still be ample. Consequently, their intersection with any curve in Y 1 ​ and Y 2 ​ must be strictly positive. In particular, for the curves m 1 ​ ∼ l 1 ​ − e 1 ​ and m 2 ​ ∼ l 2 ​ − e 2 ​ , we have: L 1 ​ ⋅ m 1 ​ > 0 and L 2 ​ ⋅ m 2 ​ > 0. By linearity, this implies: L 1 ​ ⋅ l 1 ​ > L 1 ​ ⋅ e 1 ​ and L 2 ​ ⋅ l 2 ​ > L 2 ​ ⋅ e 2 ​ . However, due to the gluing conditions, the intersection numbers evaluated on the identified curves must be equal: L 1 ​ ⋅ l 1 ​ = L 2 ​ ⋅ e 2 ​ and L 1 ​ ⋅ e 1 ​ = L 2 ​ ⋅ l 2 ​ . This immediately leads to a contradiction! (We would obtain L 1 ​ ⋅ l 1 ​ > L 1 ​ ⋅ e 1 ​ = L 2 ​ ⋅ l 2 ​ > L 2 ​ ⋅ e 2 ​ = L 1 ​ ⋅ l 1 ​ , which is impossible). Therefore, X is not projective. Since X is constructed by gluing proper schemes along proper closed subschemes, X itself is proper. This provides a classical example showing that a proper scheme is not necessarily projective.

讲义：高维代数簇 · 代数曲面的极小模型纲领 (MMP) 1 极小代数曲面 定义 1.1. 设 S 为光滑射影曲面. 若对于任一光滑射影曲面的双有理态射 π : S → S ′ 都是同构, 则称 S 为 极小代数曲面. 在这一讲, 我们的目标是证明极小曲面的一则等价刻画: “曲面上无 ( − 1 ) 曲线”. 这是意大利数学家 Guido Castelnuovo 的工作. 例 1.2. 如 P 2 与 P 1 × P 1 . 两者上的所有不可约曲线自交数都非负, 因而极小. 2 Zariski 主定理 定义 2.1. 设 f : X ⇢ Y 是射影簇间的双有理映射, 定义域为 U 0 ​ . 记 Γ 0 ​ = {( x , f ( x )) ∣ x ∈ U 0 ​ } ⊆ X × Y . 称 Γ 0 ​ ​ (在 X × Y 内取闭包) 为 f 的图像. 若 D 是 X 的闭子集, 则作 f ( D ) := ( π 2 − 1 ​ ∘ π 1 ​ ) ( D ) . 称为 D 的 完全形变 . 若 f 在 p ∈ X 处无定义, 则称 p 为 f 的 基本点 . 此时 f ( p ) 定义为其完全形变. 引理 2.2. 设 X , Y 为射影簇, 且 X 是正规的. 对于双有理映射 f : X ⇢ Y , 设定义域为 U 0 ​ , 则 codim X ​ ( X − U 0 ​ ) ≥ 2 . 定理 2.3. 设 X 是正规射影簇, f : X ⇢ Y 是射影簇间的双有理映射, p ∈ X 是基本点, 则 f ( p ) 是连通的, 且 dim f ( p ) ≥ 1 . 3 Castelnuovo 定理 定理 3.1. 设 f : X ′ → X 是光滑射影簇间的双有理态射, 且非同构. 若 p 是 f − 1 : X ⇢ X ′ 的基本点, 则 f 穿过以 p 为中心的爆破. 证明. 设 π : X ~ → X 是以 p 为中心的爆破, 例外除子为 E . 记双有理映射 g = π − 1 ∘ f : X ′ ⇢ X ~ , 我们证明 T 是态射. 否则, 取 p ‘ ∈ X ′ 为 T 的基本点, 则 f ( p ′ ) = p (由于 π − 1 在 p 以外皆有定义, 而 f 是态射) . 故 g ( p ′ ) = E . 令 U ′ = X ′ \ f − 1 ( p ) , 而 U = X \ p , 那么 π − 1 ∣ U ​ : U → U ′ 是态射, □ 推论 3.2. 设 f : X ′ → X 是光滑射影曲面间的双有理态射. 记 n ( f ) 为被 f 收缩成点的不可约曲线的条数, 则 f 可被分解为 n ( f ) 个单点爆破的复合. 证明. 由引理 2.2 , f − 1 的基本点有限, 故 n ( f ) < ∞ . 我们以归纳完成该证明. 若 n ( f ) = 0 , 那么 f 是拟有限的分离双有理态射. 由于是光滑情形, 故由 Zariski 主定理知 f 是同构. 若 n ( f ) > 0 , 那么取 f − 1 的基本点 p , 并如定理 3.1 分解 f 为 π ∘ g , 其中 π = Bl p ​ , 并记例外除子为 E . 对于 X ′ 上的不可约曲线 C , 若 g ( C ) 是单点, 那么 f ( C ) 亦是单点, 从而 n ( g ) ≤ n ( f ) . 下面我们证明这里的不等号是严格的. 若 f 将 X ′ 上的曲线 D 压缩至点 q  = p , 则 π − 1 ( q ) 也是单点. 由于 g − 1 ( E ) 是 X ~ 中有限条不可约曲线的有限和 (记 g − 1 ( E ) = k 1 ​ C 1 ​ + ⋯ + k r ​ C r ​ ) , 且 g 是打满 E 的, 故至少有一条 C i ​ 被 g 映为 E . 而 Zariski 主定理告诉我们 E 中任意一点的原像都是连通的, 故 g 恰好把一条 C i ​ 映为 E . 那么该 C i ​ 就是可被 f 收缩, 但无法被 g 收缩的曲线. 所以 n ( g ) < n ( f ) . 由归纳证毕. □ 定理 3.3. 设 f : X ′ ⇢ X 是光滑射影曲面间的双有理态射, 则 f 可分解为有限个单点爆破及其逆的复合. 定理 3.4. 设 X 是光滑射影曲面. 若 X 上有 ( − 1 ) -曲线 E , 则存在光滑射影曲面 X 1 ​ 及单点爆破 σ : X → X 1 ​ 使得其例外除子为 E . 推论 3.5. (1) 光滑射影曲面极小 当且仅当其上无 ( − 1 ) -曲线; (2) 任何光滑射影曲面都有极小模型. 4 极小模型的唯一性 定义 4.1. 设 X 为光滑代数簇. 定义 X 的小平维数为 κ ( X ) = ⎩ ⎨ ⎧ ​ − ∞ 0 max { dim ϕ ∣ m K X ​ ∣ ​ ( X ) ​ } ​ ， h 0 ( m K X ​ ) = 0∀ m ∈ N ， h 0 ( m K X ​ ) ≤ 1∀ m ∈ N ，且存在 m ∈ N 使得 h 0 ( m K X ​ ) = 1 ，其余情况 ​ . 引理 4.2. 设 S 是光滑射影曲面, κ ( S ) ≥ 0 , 则 S 是极小曲面 当且仅当 K S ​ 是 nef 的. 当曲面 S 的小平维数为 − ∞ 时, S 的极小模型一定是直纹面, 即存在到光滑曲线的约化 f : S → B , 使得对于任意 b ∈ B , f − 1 ( b ) ≅ P 1 . 定理 4.3. 设 S 为光滑射影曲面, 且 κ ( S ) ≥ 0 , 则 S 有唯一极小模型.

讲义：高维代数簇 · 曲面的有理奇点 1 有理奇点 定义 1.1. 设 p ∈ S ′ 是孤立奇点, S ′ 是正规曲面. 若存在一个奇点解消 π : S → S ′ , 使得 R i π ∗ ​ O S ​ = 0 对于任意 i > 0 成立, 则称 p 是 有理奇点 , 并称 π 是 有理解消 . 2 ADE 曲线 定义 2.1. 设 C = ∑ C i ​ ↪ S 是光滑曲面 S 上的例外曲线. 若诸 C i 2 ​ = − 2 且 C i ​ ≅ P 1 , 则称 C 为 ADE 曲线.

讲义：高维代数簇 · 纤维化与例外曲线 1 纤维化与相对极小模型 定义 1.1. 设 f : X → S 是代数簇间的紧合约化, 且 S 是正规的, 且维数满足 dim X > dim S , 则称 f 是 纤维化. 例 1.2 (Lefschetz 线束) . 设 X 是光滑射影簇, H 是 X 上的非常丰沛除子. 取子线性系统 Λ ⊂ ∣ H ∣ , 由 H 1 ​ 、 H 2 ​ 生成且 dim Λ = 1 . 称 Λ 为 Lefschetz 线束 . 该 Λ 有基点, 且 Bs ( Λ ) ⊇ H 1 ​ ∩ H 2 ​ . 爆破后得纤维化 f : X ′ → P 1 . 引理 1.3. 设 f : S → C 为纤维化, 其中 S 为光滑射影曲面, 而 C 为光滑射影曲线. 则 f 的一般纤维的亏格不依赖于纤维的选取, 并定义为 f 的亏格. 引理 1.4. 设 f : S → C 为曲面的纤维化, F 是一般纤维, 则 (1) O F ​ ( F ) ≅ O F ​ , F 2 = 0 , 且 F 是 nef 的; (2) 若 F 0 ​ = ∑ m i ​ Γ i ​ 为奇异纤维, 则 ∀ i , 有 F 0 ​ ⋅ Γ i ​ = 0 ; (3) 设 D = ∑ a i ​ Γ i ​ , a i ​ ∈ Q , 则 D 2 ≤ 0 . 等号成立 当且仅当 D 是 F 0 ​ 的有理数倍. 特别地, 设 F 0 ​ 是可约奇异纤维, 则对于 F 0 ​ 的任一不可约分支 Γ , 有自交数 Γ 2 < 0 , 即奇异纤维的不可约分支对应的相交矩阵是半负定的. 引理 1.5. 设 f : S → C 为曲面的纤维化. 记 Γ 1 ​ , … , Γ t ​ 为 f 的所有可约奇异纤维, ι ( Γ i ​ ) 为 Γ i ​ 的不可约分支数, 则 ρ ( S ) ≥ ∑ i = 1 t ​ ( ι ( Γ i ​ ) − 1 ) + 2 . 我们称纤维化 f : S → C 与 f ′ : S ′ → C 双有理等价, 是指存在双有理映射 π : S ⇢ S ′ 使得 f ′ ∘ π = f . 定义 1.6. 设 f : S → C 为曲面的纤维化. 若 f 的任意纤维中不含 ( − 1 ) -曲线, 则称 f 是 相对极小 的. 引理 1.7. 设 f : S → C 为相对极小的曲面纤维化, 而 Γ ↪ F 0 ​ 是奇异纤维 F 0 ​ 中的一个不可约分支, 则 K S ​ ⋅ Γ ≥ 0 , 且 K S ​ ⋅ Γ = 0 当且仅当 Γ 是 ( − 2 ) -曲线. 引理 1.8. 设 f : S → C 是相对极小的曲面纤维化, 且 g ( f ) ≥ 1 . 设 Γ 是 f 的纤维中的一个不可约分支, 则 K S ​ ⋅ Γ ≥ 0 . 定理 1.9. 设 f : S → C 是曲面纤维化, 则 f 必有相对极小模型. 且若 g ( f ) ≥ 1 , 则 f 的相对极小模型唯一. 2 例外曲线 定义 2.1. 设 S 是光滑曲面. 若存在正规曲面 S ′ 及双有理态射 π : S → S ′ 以及 S 上的曲线 E 满足: (1) π ( E ) 是 S ′ 上的一个闭点; (2) π ∣ S \ E ​ : S \ E → S ′ \ π ( E ) 是同构, 则称 E 为态射 π 的例外曲线. 引理 2.2. 设 S 是光滑曲面, 而 S ′ 是正规射影曲面. 若 E = ∑ E i ​ 是态射 π : S → S ′ 的例外曲线, 则相交矩阵 ( E i ​ ⋅ E j ​ ) 负定. 引理 2.3. 设 S 是光滑曲面. C i ​ 是 S 上的不可约曲线, m i ​ ∈ Z > 0 ​ . 设除子 F = ∑ m i ​ C i ​ , 且诸 F ⋅ C i ​ ≤ 0 . 那么对于除子 D = ∑ r i ​ C i ​  = 0 , 其中 r i ​ ∈ Q , 有: (1) D 2 ≤ 0 . 由 D 的任意性, 这即相交矩阵 ( C i ​ ⋅ C j ​ ) 半负定; (2) 若 F 连通, 且 D 2 = 0 , 则 D 是 F 的有理数倍, 且诸 F ⋅ C i ​ = 0 . 命题 2.4. 若 E ↪ S 是例外曲线, 则对于任意 m i ​ ≥ 0 , 有 h 0 ( ∑ m i ​ E i ​ ) = 1 . 定义 2.5. 设 L 是 S 上的除子. 若存在 m ∈ Z > 0 ​ 使得 ∣ m L ∣ 无基点, 则称 L 是 半丰沛 的. 定理 2.6. 设 S 是光滑射影曲面, L 是 S 上的半丰沛大除子, 则存在正规射影曲面 Z 与双有理态射 π : S → Z 、正整数 m 0 ​ Z 上的丰沛除子 H , 使得 m 0 ​ L ∼ π ∗ H . 这时, 称 π 是 L 的半丰沛纤维化.

笔记：表示论专题 · 2026.3.4 1 Set up for sheaf theory There are four common settings for the study of sheaves in algebraic geometry and representation theory: 1. Betti setting: We consider complex analytic spaces endowed with the classical topology (not the Zariski topology). Note: We will exclusively focus on this setting for the duration of this course. 2. Étale setting over C : We consider complex varieties equipped with the étale topology, using l -adic coefficients. This topology acts as a remedy for the topological shortcomings of the Zariski topology. 3. Algebraic (de Rham) setting: We consider complex varieties endowed with the Zariski topology. This setting heavily relies on the theory of D -modules (which behave significantly differently from standard coherent sheaves). 4. Positive characteristic setting: We consider varieties defined over a finite field F q ​ , equipped with the étale topology and using l -adic coefficients. Relations: • Why not use C -sheaves on the Zariski topology? 引理 1.1. Any locally constant sheaf on an irreducible topological space is constant. 注 1.2. The Zariski topology has too few open sets, making it inconvenient to use sheaves to study topological properties. 2 Local Systems 定义 2.1. A local system (of C -vector spaces) on a topological space X is a locally constant sheaf. i.e., ∀ x ∈ X , ∃ open x ∈ U ⊂ X such that F ∣ U ​ is constant. 例 2.2. Let X = C ∖ { 0 } , for any U ⊂ X : F ( U ) = { holomorphic functions f on U ∣ ∂ z ​ f = 2 z 1 ​ f } then F is a local system and we can find F x ​ ≅ C z 1/2 ∀ x ∈ X . But z 1/2 can’t be defined on X , so F is not a constant sheaf. 引理 2.3. Any local system on [ 0 , 1 ] is constant. Proof. Let L be a local system on [ 0 , 1 ] (compact). There exists a finite open covering [ 0 , 1 ] = ⋃ i ​ U i ​ such that L ∣ U i ​ ​ is constant. We may assume the finite open covering consists of intervals U i ​ = ( a i ​ , b i ​ ) (or half-open intervals like [ 0 , b i ​ ) and ( a i ​ , 1 ] ) such that b i ​ ∈ U i + 1 ​ . For example, let U 1 ​ = [ 0 , b 1 ​ ) and U 2 ​ = ( a 2 ​ , b 2 ​ ) , so that their intersection is U 1 ​ ∩ U 2 ​ = ( a 2 ​ , b 1 ​ ) , and so forth. We consider the restriction maps: L ( U 1 ​ ) ≅ ​ L ( U 1 ​ ∩ U 2 ​ ) ≅ ​ L ( U 2 ​ ) . This implies that the local system L is constant on the union U 1 ​ ∪ U 2 ​ . By continuing this process with induction, we conclude that L is constant on the entire interval [ 0 , 1 ] . □ Similarly, any local system on [ 0 , 1 ] × [ 0 , 1 ] is constant. 引理 2.4. For any continuous map f : X → Y and a local system L on Y , the pullback f ∗ L is a local system on X . Proof. Locally, the pullback functor f ∗ sends a constant sheaf to a constant sheaf. □ 3 Monodromy representations Let Loc ( X ) denote the category of local systems on X . 命题 3.1. For a locally connected topological space X , Loc ( X ) is an abelian category. Fix a base point x 0 ​ ∈ X . Our goal is to construct a functor Loc ( X ) ⟶ Rep ( π 1 ​ ( X , x 0 ​ )) where Rep ( π 1 ​ ( X , x 0 ​ )) represents the category of finite dimensional representations {( V , π 1 ​ ( X , x 0 ​ ) → GL ( V ))} . For any path γ : [ 0 , 1 ] → X and any local system L ∈ Loc ( X ) , note that the pullback γ ∗ L is constant on [ 0 , 1 ] by the previous lemma. This gives us a natural isomorphism ρ ( γ ) through the global sections Γ ([ 0 , 1 ] , γ ∗ L ) . Specifically, we have the following identifications of stalks: L γ ( 1 ) ​ = ( γ ∗ L ) 1 ​ ≅ ​ Γ ([ 0 , 1 ] , γ ∗ L ) ≅ ​ ( γ ∗ L ) 0 ​ = L γ ( 0 ) ​ . For a loop where γ ( 0 ) = γ ( 1 ) = x 0 ​ , we obtain an isomorphism ρ ( γ ) : L x 0 ​ ​ ≅ ​ L x 0 ​ ​ . That is, ρ ( γ ) ∈ GL ( L x 0 ​ ​ ) . 引理 3.2. The assignment ρ ( γ ) induces a well-defined action of the fundamental group π 1 ​ ( X , x 0 ​ ) on the vector space V = L x 0 ​ ​ . Proof. To show that this action is well-defined, we need to verify the following properties: 1. If γ is the identity path, then ρ ( γ ) is the identity isomorphism. 2. The assignment respects path composition. 3. The assignment is invariant under homotopy. That is, if two paths are homotopic ( γ ∼ γ ′ ), then their induced isomorphisms are equal, meaning ρ ( γ ) = ρ ( γ ′ ) . To prove the homotopy invariance, let H : [ 0 , 1 ] × [ 0 , 1 ] → X be a homotopy between γ and γ ′ , such that H ( t , 0 ) = γ ( t ) and H ( t , 1 ) = γ ′ ( t ) . Since the pullback H ∗ L is a constant local system on the square [ 0 , 1 ] × [ 0 , 1 ] , its restriction to the boundary paths is also constant. This yields γ ∗ L = γ ′ ∗ L , which implies that ρ ( γ ) = ρ ( γ ′ ) . □ We have thus defined the monodromy representation functor: Mon x 0 ​ ​ : Loc ( X ) L ​ ⟶ Rep ( π 1 ​ ( X , x 0 ​ )) ⟼ L x 0 ​ ​ . ​ 例 3.3. Consider the previous example of the local system associated with z 1/2 on X = C ∖ { 0 } . Let the base point be x 0 ​ = 1 . The fundamental group is π 1 ​ ( X , x 0 ​ ) ≅ Z . The monodromy representation maps the generator of the fundamental group to an element in GL ( C ) ≅ C ∗ . Specifically, as z goes around the origin once, the branch of z 1/2 changes sign, so the generator 1 ∈ Z is mapped to − 1 ∈ C ∗ (i.e., z 1/2 ↦ − z 1/2 ). 定理 3.4. Suppose the topological space X is connected, locally path-connected, and locally simply-connected. Then the monodromy functor Mon x 0 ​ ​ is an equivalence of categories. 注 3.5. For example, topological manifolds satisfy these local conditions. In addition, cones also satisfy these local conditions. Fact : For the inverse functor, Let p : X ~ → X be the universal covering space. The fundamental group π 1 ​ ( X , x 0 ​ ) acts on X ~ via deck transformations on the fibers of p . Given a representation V ∈ Rep ( π 1 ​ ( X , x 0 ​ )) , we define a presheaf L V ​ by assigning to each open set U ⊆ X : L V ​ ( U ) = { locally constant, π 1 ​ ( X , x 0 ​ ) -equivariant maps ϕ : p − 1 ( U ) → V i.e., ϕ ( g ⋅ y ) = g ⋅ ϕ ( y ) for any g ∈ π 1 ​ ( X , x 0 ​ ) and y ∈ p − 1 ( U ) ​ } . ​ One can verify that L V ​ is indeed a sheaf. Furthermore, we have an isomorphism on the stalk at the base point: ( L V ​ ) x 0 ​ ​ ≅ V . And for any local system L , we have L L x 0 ​ ​ ​ ≅ L . ( Hint: Fix a point x ~ 0 ​ ∈ p − 1 ( x 0 ​ ) . For any x ∈ X , fix a path α x ​ from x 0 ​ to x (fixing this data ensures consistency), with the condition that the chosen path for the base point α x 0 ​ ​ is the identity path.) 引理 3.6. Let X be as in the previous theorem (which implies X is path-connected). For any local system L ∈ Loc ( X ) corresponding to a representation V ∈ Rep ( π 1 ​ ( X , x 0 ​ )) , there is an isomorphism of global sections: Γ ( X , L ) ≅ V π 1 ​ ( X , x 0 ​ ) . Proof. We have a natural evaluation map Γ ( X , L ) → L x 0 ​ ​ = V . For any loop γ ∈ π 1 ​ ( X , x 0 ​ ) where γ ( 0 ) = γ ( 1 ) = x 0 ​ , the monodromy action is given by the composition of isomorphisms: ρ ( γ ) : V = L x 0 ​ ​ ≅ ​ Γ ([ 0 , 1 ] , γ ∗ L ) ≅ ​ L x 0 ​ ​ . For any global section s ∈ Γ ( X , L ) , its pullback along the loop yields s ∣ [ 0 , 1 ] ​ ∈ Γ ([ 0 , 1 ] , γ ∗ L ) . This implies that ρ ( γ ) ( s x 0 ​ ​ ) = s x 0 ​ ​ . Thus, the image of the evaluation map lies in the invariant subspace V π 1 ​ ( X , x 0 ​ ) . To show this map is an isomorphism, we prove injectivity and surjectivity separately: • Injectivity: For any two global sections s , s ′ ∈ Γ ( X , L ) , suppose their stalks at x 0 ​ are equal, meaning s x 0 ​ ​ = s x 0 ​ ′ ​ . For any arbitrary point x ∈ X , take a path α such that α ( 0 ) = x 0 ​ and α ( 1 ) = x . This path induces an isomorphism ρ ( α ) : L x 0 ​ ​ ≅ ​ L x ​ . Because s and s ′ are global sections, we have ρ ( α ) ( s x 0 ​ ​ ) = s x ​ and ρ ( α ) ( s x 0 ​ ′ ​ ) = s x ′ ​ . Given that s x 0 ​ ​ = s x 0 ​ ′ ​ , it follows immediately that s x ​ = s x ′ ​ . Since x is arbitrary, we conclude that s = s ′ . • Surjectivity: Let v ∈ V π 1 ​ ( X , x 0 ​ ) be an invariant element. For any x ∈ X , take a path α from x 0 ​ to x . This path induces an isomorphism ρ ( α ) : L x 0 ​ ​ ≅ ​ L x ​ . We can define the stalk at x by setting v x ​ := ρ ( α ) ( v ) . Because v is invariant under the action of the fundamental group π 1 ​ ( X , x 0 ​ ) , this definition is independent of the choice of the path α . This process yields a well-defined global section s ∈ Γ ( X , L ) such that s x 0 ​ ​ = v . □ 4 Constructible Sheaves It is not enough to consider the category of local systems Loc ( X ) for the following reasons: 1. It only detects the fundamental group π 1 ​ ( X , x 0 ​ ) . 2. It is not stable under functors. 例 4.1. Let L be the local system associated with z 1/2 on X = C ∖ { 0 } . Consider the inclusion map j : X ↪ Y = C , and the pushforward sheaf j ∗ ​ L on Y . Let us compute the stalk at the origin: ( j ∗ ​ L ) 0 ​ = 0 ∈ V ⊆ Y lim ​ ​ ( j ∗ ​ L ) ( V ) = 0 ∈ V lim ​ ​ L ( V ∖ { 0 }) = 0. Since the stalk at 0 is zero but the stalks elsewhere are non-zero, the sheaf j ∗ ​ L is not a local system on Y . Thus, j ∗ ​ L ∈ / Loc ( Y ) . 定义 4.2. A stratification of a topological space X is a finite collection of subspaces ( X i ​ ) i ∈ I ​ of X , called strata , such that: 1. X = ⋃ i ∈ I ​ X i ​ . 2. X i ​ ∩ X j ​ = ∅ for any i  = j . 3. Every stratum X i ​ is a connected topological manifold. 4. Every stratum X i ​ is locally closed in X . 5. If X i ​ ∩ X j ​ ​  = ∅ , then X i ​ ⊆ X j ​ ​ . (This is equivalent to the frontier condition: the boundary ∂ X i ​ = X i ​ ​ ∖ X i ​ is a union of some strata X j ​ ). 注 4.3. When X is an algebraic variety, we require that each stratum X i ​ is a smooth, connected, Zariski locally closed subvariety. 定义 4.4. A refinement of a stratification X = ⨆ i ∈ I ​ X i ​ is another stratification X = ⨆ j ∈ J ​ X j ​ such that every stratum X j ​ is contained in some stratum X i ​ . 例 4.5. 1. If X is a manifold, then it has a trivial stratification X = X 1 ​ . 2. Let X = {( x , y ) ∈ C 2 ∣ x y = 0 } ⊂ C 2 . We can stratify X as: X = { 0 } ⊔ ( X ∖ { 0 }) = { 0 } ⊔ ( x -axis ∖ { 0 }) ⊔ ( y -axis ∖ { 0 }) . 3. Let G be an algebraic group (for example, GL n ​ ( C ) ) and X be an algebraic variety equipped with a G -action that has finitely many orbits. This naturally induces a stratification X = ⨆ ( G -orbits ) . As a specific case, consider the general linear group GL n ​ ( C ) acting by conjugation on the nilpotent cone N = { A ∈ M n × n ​ ( C ) ∣ A n = 0 } . The set of orbits ∣ GL n ​ ( C ) ∖ N ∣ is in bijection with the set of partitions of n . 引理 4.6. Let X be an algebraic variety. 1. Any two stratifications of X have a common refinement. 2. For any locally closed subvariety Y ⊆ X , Y is a union of strata for some stratification of X . Proof. (1) This is left as a homework exercise. The general strategy is to consider the smooth locus of the variety and proceed using Noetherian induction. (2) The proof follows a similar idea. □ 注 4.7. In more general topological settings, there exist certain regularity conditions one might need to impose on a stratification, such as the Whitney stratification conditions. However, we can safely avoid these technical conditions when we are working exclusively with algebraic varieties. 定义 4.8. Let X be a topological space equipped with a stratification ( X i ​ ) i ∈ I ​ . A sheaf F on X is weakly constructible with respect to I if its restriction F ∣ X i ​ ​ ∈ Loc ( X i ​ ) for all i ∈ I . A sheaf is simply called weakly constructible if it is weakly constructible with respect to some stratification I . Furthermore, a sheaf is constructible (with respect to I ) if, moreover, for all i ∈ I , the restriction F ∣ X i ​ ​ is of finite rank (i.e., all of its stalks are finite-dimensional vector spaces). We denote the category of constructible sheaves on X (with respect to a fixed stratification I ) by Sh c ​ ( X ) (respectively, Sh I ​ ( X ) ). 例 4.9. 1. If X is a smooth variety, then the category of finite-rank local systems Loc fin ( X ) is a subcategory of Sh c ​ ( X ) . 2. For the local system L associated with z 1/2 on C ∖ { 0 } , let j : C ∖ { 0 } ↪ C be the inclusion map. Then the pushforward sheaf j ∗ ​ L belongs to Sh c ​ ( X ) (where X = C ). On derived categories: 定义 4.10. A complex of sheaves F ∙ is called (weakly) constructible (with respect to I ) if its k -th cohomology sheaf H k ( F ∙ ) satisfies the same property for all k ∈ Z . We denote the corresponding derived categories as D I b ​ ( X ) ⊆ D b ( X ) and D c b ​ ( X ) ⊆ D b ( X ) , where D b ( X ) stands for the bounded derived category of sheaves on X . Both D I b ​ ( X ) and D c b ​ ( X ) form full triangulated subcategories. There is a natural functor connecting the derived category of constructible sheaves to the constructible derived category: D b ( Sh c ​ ( X )) ⟶ D c b ​ ( X ) . 定理 4.11. For any complex algebraic variety X , the natural functor from the bounded derived category of constructible sheaves to the constructible derived category, D b ( Sh c ​ ( X )) ≃ ​ D c b ​ ( X ) , is an equivalence of categories. If Y is ϕ -related to X (i.e. Y ϕ ( p ) ​ = ( D p ​ ϕ ) ( X p ​ ) , ∀ p ∈ M ), prove that ( L Y ​ f ) ∘ ϕ = L X ​ ( f ∘ ϕ ) , ∀ f ∈ C ∞ ( N ) . • If X ′ is ϕ -related to Y , prove that [ X ′ , Y ′ ] is ϕ -related to [ X , Y ] . Solution: If Y ϕ ( p ) ​ = ( D p ​ ϕ ) X p ​ , ∀ p ∈ M , then ( L Y ​ f ) ∘ ϕ ( p ) ​ = ( D ϕ ( p ) ​ f ) ( Y ϕ ( p ) ​ ) = ( D ϕ ( p ) ​ f ) ( D p ​ ϕ ) ( X p ​ ) = (( D p ​ ϕ ) X p ​ ) ( f ) = L X ​ ( f ∘ ϕ ) ( p ) . ​ Hence X ′ Y ′ ( f ∘ ϕ ) = X ′ (( Y f ) ∘ ϕ ) = ( X Y f ) ∘ ϕ ; similarly, Y ′ X ′ ( f ∘ ϕ ) = ( Y X f ) ∘ ϕ . Therefore, [ X ′ , Y ′ ] ( f ∘ ϕ ) ​ = X ′ Y ′ ( f ∘ ϕ ) − Y ′ X ′ ( f ∘ ϕ ) = ( X Y f ) ∘ ϕ − ( Y X f ) ∘ ϕ = ([ X , Y ] f ) ∘ ϕ . ​ Question 2. Show that • GL ( n , R ) is a non-compact Lie group of n 2 dimension; • GL ( n , C ) is a non-compact Lie group of 2 n 2 dimension; • both of them are non-abelian for n ≥ 2 . Solution: Let M ( n , R ) denote the set of n × n matrices with real entries. Because it is a real vector space of dimension n 2 under matrix addition and scalar multiplication, M ( n , R ) is a smooth n 2 -dimensional smooth manifold. Now GL ( n , R ) is an open subset of M ( n , R ) , namely the set where det : M ( n , R ) → R is nonzero, hence GL ( n , R ) is a smooth n 2 -dimensional submanifold of M ( n , R ) . Moreover, for all x ∈ GL ( n , R ) , λ x ∈ GL ( n , R ) ( λ ∈ R − { 0 }) . Therefore GL ( n , R ) is not bounded, hence non-compact. Next we prove that GL ( n , R ) admits a Lie group structure. Multiplication is smooth because the matrix entries of a product matrix A B are polynomials in the entries of A and B . Inversion is smooth by Cramer’s Rule. When n ≥ 2 , A B  = B A , hence GL ( n , R ) is not Abelian when n ≥ 2 . The case for GL ( n , C ) is similar. Question 3. Find an explicit Lie group homomorphism ϕ : S U ( 3 ) × S U ( 2 ) × U ( 1 ) → S U ( 5 ) with discrete kernel. Solution: Consider the homomorphism ϕ : S U ( 3 ) × S U ( 2 ) × U ( 1 ) → S U ( 5 ) ( U 3 ​ , U 2 ​ , e i θ ) ↦ ( e − 2 i θ U 3 ​ 0 ​ 0 e 3 i θ U 2 ​ ​ ) . ​ • ϕ is indeed a Lie group homomorphism. ϕ is clearly a group homomorphism; to prove ϕ is smooth, note just ϕ ( U 3 ​ , U 2 ​ , e i θ ) = diag { e − 2 i θ , e − 2 i θ , e − 2 i θ , e 3 i θ , e 3 i θ } ( U 3 ​ 0 ​ 0 U 2 ​ ​ ) . The two terms of the left hand side of the above equation are embeddings of U ( 1 ) and S U ( 3 ) × S U ( 2 ) into S U ( 5 ) , respectively. Hence they are smooth; but also product operation in Lie group is smooth, so ϕ is smooth. • The kernel of ϕ is discrete. If ( U 3 ​ , U 2 ​ , e i θ ) ∈ Ker ϕ , then U 3 ​ = diag { e 2 i θ , e 2 i θ , e 2 i θ } , U 2 ​ = diag { e − 3 i θ , e − 3 i θ } . Moreover, U 3 ​ ∈ S U ( 3 ) , U 2 ​ ∈ S U ( 2 ) implies e 6 i θ = 1 , which means that the possible values of θ are taken from { 3 nπ ​ : n ∈ Z } , which is discrete. Question 4. Let K = R , C and identify the Lie algebra of an embedded Lie subgroup of GL ( n , K ) with a Lie subalgebra of Mat ( n × n , K ) . Prove that • The Lie bracket on the Lie subalgebra of Mat ( n × n , K ) is the standard commutator of matrices. • The Lie algebras of classical groups are the following Lie subalgebras of Mat ( n × n , K ) . sl ( n , K ) = { M ∈ Mat ( n × n , K ) : tr ( M ) = 0 } , o ( n ) = { M ∈ Mat ( n × n , K ) : M + M T = 0 } , u ( n ) = { M ∈ Mat ( n × n , K ) : M + M † = 0 } , so ( n ) = o ( n ) , su ( n ) = { M ∈ Mat ( n × n , K ) : M + M † = 0 , tr ( M ) = 0 } . [Hint : Use the fact that ‘If H is an embedded Lie subgroup of G , then h is an embedded Lie subalgebra of g ’ and compute the dimension of each matrix group.] See [ Ha17 ] Theorem 1.5.22 and 1.5.27. Question 5. Let X ∈ g and g ∈ G with ( G , g ) lying in {( S L ( n , K ) , sl ( n , K )) , ( O ( n ) , o ( n )) , ( U ( n ) , u ( n )) , ( SO ( n ) , so ( n )) , ( S U ( n ) , su ( n ))} . Show that g is closed under the map X ↦ g ⋅ X ⋅ g − 1 . Solution: Use Question 4 and DIRECT calculation. Question 6. Let G be a connected Lie group. Define the centre of G as Z ( G ) := { g ∈ G : g h = h g , ∀ h ∈ G } . Prove that • Z ( G ) is the kernel of the adjoint representation Ad G ​ . • Z ( G ) is an embedded Lie subgroup in G with Lie algebra given by the centre z ( g ) of g . • g is abelian if and only if G is abelian. • Ad G ​ is trivial (i.e. every element of G is mapped to the identity) if and only if G is abelian. • The left-invariant and right-invariant vector fields on a connected Lie group G coincide if and only if G is abelian. Solution: Suppose that Ad g ​ is trivial, and let h = exp ( v ) ∈ G . Now γ ( t ) = g ⋅ exp ⋅ g − 1 is a curve in G whose velocity at t = 0 is Ad g ​ ( v ) = v , since Ad g ​ is trivial. However, ρ ( t ) = exp ( t v ) is also a curve in G with initial velocity v , and by the uniqueness of integral curve, g ⋅ exp ( t v ) ⋅ g − 1 = exp ( t v ) . In particular, when t = 1 one has g h = h g . For general h ∈ G , since G is connected, by Proposition 7.14 of [ Lee13 ], h can always be written as h = exp ( v 1 ​ ) ⋯ exp ( v k ​ ) , and the commutativity comes from iterating what we have done above. Hence Ker ( Ad g ​ ) ⊂ Z ( G ) . On the other hand elements of Z ( G ) clearly fall into Ker ( Ad G ​ ) . Therefore Ker ( Ad G ​ ) = Z ( G ) . Now by Proposition 20.8 of [ Lee13 ], we have a commutative diagram Since Ker ( Ad G ​ ) = Z ( G ) , the Lie algebra z ( g ) of Z ( G ) is given by Ker ( ad g ​ ) = { X ∈ g : [ X , Y ] = 0 , ∀ Y ∈ g } . In order this correspondence behaves well, one must demonstrate that Z ( G ) is a closed subgroup of G . For this, let C g ​ = { g 1 ​ ∈ G : g 1 ​ g = g g 1 ​ } . Then C g ​ is the preimage f − 1 ({ e }) where f is the smooth map f ( g 1 ​ ) := g g 1 ​ g − 1 g 1 − 1 ​ . Therefore, C g ​ is closed, and then Z ( G ) = ∩ g ∈ G ​ C g ​ is a closed subgroup of G . The fact that Λ is invertible is a consequence of introducing the Hilbert structure F on the space of initial data. The difficulty, then, lies in establishing the uniqueness theorem. Finally, two concluding remarks are in order. Q Does the time T play any role in the problem? A Yes. Recall that as a hyperbolic system, the effect of boundary data (here the control v ) is of finite propagation speed. So T has to be taken sufficiently large . ( T is not big enough in the picture, as the shaded cone of dependence at ( x 0 , T ) does not touch ∂ Ω × ( 0 , T ) .) Q Are the spaces F , F ′ necessarily abstract? A Surely not. 笔记：金融中的随机分析 We make the following assumptions throughout. • There is a probability triple ( Ω , F , P ) where ∘ P is the “true” or physical probability measure ∘ Ω is the universe of possible outcomes. We use ω ∈ Ω to represent a generic outcome, typically a sample path(s) of a stochastic process(es). ∘ the set F represents the set of possible events where an event is a subset of Ω . • There is also a filtration, { F t ​ } t ≥ 0 ​ , that models the evolution of information through time. So for example, if it is known by time t whether or not an event, E , has occurred, then we have E ∈ F t ​ . If we are working with a finite horizon, [ 0 , T ] , then we can take F = F T ​ . • We also say that a stochastic process, X t ​ , is F t ​ -adapted if the value of X t ​ is known at time t when the information represented by F t ​ is known. All the processes we consider will be F t ​ -adapted so we will not bother to state this in the sequel. • In the continuous-time models that we will study, it will be understood that the filtration { F t ​ } t ≥ 0 ​ will be the filtration generated by the stochastic processes (usually a Brownian motion, W t ​ ) that are specified in the model description. 1 Martingales and Brownian Motion Definition 1.1. A stochastic process, { W t ​ : 0 ≤ t ≤ ∞ } , is a standard Brownian motion if 1. W 0 ​ = 0 2. It has continuous sample paths 3. It has independent, normally-distributed increments. Definition 1.2. An n -dimensional process, W t ​ = ( W t ( 1 ) ​ , … , W t ( n ) ​ ) , is a standard n -dimensional Brownian motion if each W t ( i ) ​ is a standard Brownian motion and the W t ( i ) ​ ’s are independent of each other. Definition 1.3. A stochastic process, { X t ​ : 0 ≤ t ≤ ∞ } , is a martingale with respect to the filtration, F t ​ , and probability measure, P , if 1. E P ∣∣ X t ​ ∣∣ < ∞ for all t ≥ 0 2. The Feynman-Kac Theorem plays an important role in financial engineering as it enables us to compute the prices of derivative securities (which can be expressed as expectations according to martingale pricing theory) by solving a PDE instead. It is worth mentioning, however, that in the development of derivatives pricing theory, the PDE approach preceded the martingale approach. In particular we obtain p t ​ + μ ( t , x ) p x ​ + 2 1 ​ σ 2 ( t , x ) p xx ​ = 0 for t < s . (Kolmogorov’s Backward Equation) ( 24 ) It is worth emphasizing that (24) does not always admit a unique solution. In particular boundary conditions need to be specified. For example absorbing and reflecting Brownian motions both satisfy (24) but they are very different processes. It is also worth mentioning that (23) itself is what people sometimes have in mind when they refer to Kolmogorov’s backward equation. In order to state Kolmogorov’s forward equation we must now view p ( t , x ; s , y ) as a function of ( s , y ) and therefore keep ( t , x ) fixed. It can be shown that p s ​ + ( μ ( s , y ) p ) y ​ − 2 1 ​ ( σ 2 ( t , y ) p ) yy ​ = 0 for s > t . (Kolmogorov’s Forward Equation) ( 25 ) with the initial condition p = δ x ​ ( y ) at s = t . The forward equation can be derived quickly in a formal manner from the backward equation using integration by parts but doing so rigorously can be very challenging. In fact, depending on technical and boundary conditions the forward equation (25) may not actually be satisfied. The forward equation plays a key role in local volatility models of security prices where it is used to derive the Dupire formula . 10 Change of Probability Measure The majority of financial engineering models price securities using the EMM, Q , that corresponds to taking the cash account, B t ​ , as numeraire. We use S t ​ to denote the time t price of a risky asset and B t ​ to denote the time t value of the cash account. For ease of exposition we will initially assume that the risky asset does not pay dividends. Let ϕ t ( s ) ​ and ϕ t ( b ) ​ denote the number of units of the security and cash account, respectively, that is held in a portfolio at time t . Then the value of the portfolio at time t is given by V t ​ = ϕ t ( s ) ​ S t ​ + ϕ t ( b ) ​ B t ​ . Definition 13.1. We say ϕ t ​ := ( ϕ t ( s ) ​ , ϕ t ( b ) ​ ) is self-financing if d V t ​ = ϕ t ( s ) ​ d S t ​ + ϕ t ( b ) ​ d B t ​ . Note that this definition is consistent with our definition for discrete-time models. It is also worth emphasizing the mathematical content of this definition. Note that Itô’s Lemma implies d V t ​ = ϕ t ( s ) ​ d S t ​ + ϕ t ( b ) ​ d B t ​ + A S t ​ d ϕ t ( s ) ​ + B t ​ d ϕ t ( b ) ​ ​ ​ + d S t ​ d ϕ t ( s ) ​ + d B t ​ d ϕ t ( b ) ​ so that the self-financing assumption amounts to assuming that the sum of the terms in A are identically zero. Our definitions of arbitrage , numeraire securities , equivalent martingale measures and complete markets is unchanged from the discrete-time setup. We now state without proof the two fundamental theorems of asset pricing. These results mirror those from the discrete-time theory. Theorem 13.2. (The First Fundamental Theorem of Asset Pricing) There is no arbitrage if and only if there exists an EMM, Q . A consequence of Theorem 13.2 is that in the absence of arbitrage, the deflated value process, V t ​ / N t ​ , of any self-financing trading strategy is a Q -martingale. This implies that the deflated price of any attainable security can be computed as the Q -expectation of the terminal deflated value of the security. Theorem 13.3. (The Second Fundamental Theorem of Asset Pricing) Assume there exists a security with strictly positive price process and that there are no arbitrage opportunities. Then the market is complete if and only if there exists exactly one risk-neutral martingale measure, Q . Beyond their theoretical significance, these theorems are also important in practice. If our model is complete then we can price securities with the unique EMM that accompanies it, assuming of course the absence of arbitrage. This is the case for the Black-Scholes model as well as local volatility models. If our model is incomplete then we generally work directly under an EMM, Q , which is then calibrated to market data. In particular, the true data-generating probability measure, P , is often completely ignored when working with incomplete models. In some sense the issue of completeness then only arises when we discuss replicating or hedging strategies. Here W t o ​ is a Brownian motion process defined on a probability space ( Ω , F , P o ) . The parameter σ is the volatility and α is the mean rate of growth . The market also has a risk-free asset or ”bond” with constant interest rate r : d B t ​ = r B t ​ d t , or B t ​ = B 0 ​ e r t . This model originated with the work of Black, Scholes and Merton. Its shortcomings as a model of the real market have been discussed in the literature, and various modifications have been considered. Our purpose is not to decide on the most accurate model. Without intending to diminish their importance, we are not covering models involving multiple stocks, state-dependent or stochastic volatility, incomplete markets, regime switching, jump-diffusions, or Lévy processes. Nor are we considering model calibration or parameter estimation. Instead our purpose is to use the the simple Black-Scholes model as a ”laboratory” in which to learn various techniques for calculating the prices of financial derivatives based on the no-arbitrage principle. The methods we learn here can be adapted to more complex models, though we will not pursue that. No-Arbitrage and Risk-Neutral Pricing Suppose we have a (European-style) derivative asset whose value at expiry ( t = T ) is given by a random variable X . The problem is to determine the market price V t ​ of this asset at times t < T . The absence of arbitrage in the market implies the following general risk-neutral pricing formula : V t ​ = e r t E [ e − r T X ∣ F t ​ ] . ( 1.2 ) The critical feature here is that the expectation is not calculated under the original probability measure P o but with respect to the the risk-neutral probability measure, which is characterized by the property that the discounted stock price, e − r t S t ​ , is a martingale. We will use P for that risk-neutral probability. It will be the underlying probability measure throughout; we will have virtually no need for the original P o . The hypotheses on which the formula (1.2) is based are as follows. • The description of S t ​ and B t ​ is appropriate, and the values of α , r , and σ are known. • There are no transaction costs associated with buying and selling shares of stock or bond. Stock and bond may be held in any amounts (not limited to integral multiples or positive amounts) and can be traded continuously. • The stock pays no dividends. • For any time t ≤ T knowledge of the stock price history { S u ​ : u ≤ t } constitutes complete knowledge of the state of the market at time t . (I.e. there are no stochastic components of the model other than S t ​ . The values of all market variables at time t are prescribed by knowledge of the stock price history.) The σ -algebra F t ​ is determined (or ”generated”) by this information. • X is F T ​ measurable and E [ X 2 ] < ∞ . (Remember, this is with respect to the risk-neutral probability P .) • There are no arbitrage opportunities in the market. (Mathematically, this follows from the existence of the risk-neutral probability measure.) An outline of how this leads to (1.2) is as follows. The effect of switching to the risk-neutral probability P is that the original W t o ​ is no longer a Brownian motion. Instead W t ​ = W t o ​ + ( σ α − r ​ ) t ( 1.3 ) is a Brownian motion with respect to P . The equation for the stock price process can be reformulated as d S t ​ = r S t ​ d t + σ S t ​ d W t ​ . ( 1.4 ) The solution can be written explicitly: S t ​ = S 0 ​ e ( r − σ 2 /2 ) t + σ W t ​ . Suppose that h t B ​ and h t S ​ comprise a self-financing portfolio with value process V t ​ , V t ​ d V t ​ ​ = h t B ​ B t ​ + h t S ​ S t ​ = h t B ​ d B t ​ + h t S ​ d S t ​ , ​ and which replicates X at time T : V T ​ = X . (This is always possible in the Black-Scholes model provided E [ X 2 ] < ∞ , by the completeness property and the martingale representation theorem.) Then it turns out that the discounted asset price M t ​ = V t ​ / B t ​ is also a Q -martingale. This is because its stochastic differential works out to be d M t ​ = σ h t S ​ B t ​ S t ​ ​ d W t ​ , with no d t term. By the absence of arbitrage, V t ​ must agree with the market value at time t of the contingent claim. The risk neutral formula (1.2) is just the statement of this martingale property: M t ​ = E [ M T ​ ∣ F t ​ ] , which we can rewrite as V t ​ = B t ​ E [ X / B t ​ ∣ F t ​ ] . Introduction to Partial Differential Equations To begin we want to place the Black-Scholes equation in the standard taxonomy of partial differential equations. The Black-Scholes PDE is a second order , linear , homogeneous equation. It is second order because the highest partial derivative involved is of second order. It is linear because the partial derivatives v s ​ , v ss ​ , v t ​ occur simply multiplied by known functions of the independent variables ( s and t ) and then added. In general a second order linear PDE for a function u ( x , t ) takes the form a u xx ​ + b u x t ​ + c u tt ​ + d u x ​ + e u t ​ + f u + g = 0. ( 2.3 ) The coefficients are (prescribed) functions of the independent variables: a = a ( x , t ) , … , g = g ( x , t ) . When g = 0 the equation is homogeneous. The problem is to find the function(s) u ( x , t ) which solve (2.3) for ( x , t ) in some region, usually in conjunction with some other “boundary conditions,” i.e. properties or values of the function which are specified on the boundary of the region. For (2.1) the region we are interested is the vertical strip 0 ≤ t ≤ T , 0 < s and the boundary condition is the requirement that v ( s , T ) = ϕ ( s ) for all s > 0 . There is no boundary condition specified for s = 0 (or t = 0 ); later in this chapter we will see why this is so. Assuming that a , b , and c are not all zero (else the equation would not be second order), equations of the form (2.3) are usually categorized as one of three types: hyperbolic, parabolic, or elliptic. The best known examples of each type are the following. • Wave Equation (hyperbolic): u xx ​ − u tt ​ = 0 . • Heat Equation (parabolic): u xx ​ − u t ​ = 0 . • Laplace Equation (elliptic): u xx ​ + u yy ​ = 0 . Each of the three basic PDEs above has been thoroughly studied. Other equations of the same type (hyperbolic, parabolic, or elliptic) typically share many of the same properties as the appropriate one of these examples. The Black-Scholes equation is parabolic. In fact it is fully equivalent to the heat equation by means of a change of variables which we will work out in the next section. This is very convenient for us, because every question we might ask about the Black-Scholes equation can be translated into an analogous question about the heat equation. We can then turn to the extensive literature concerning the heat equation (or parabolic PDEs in general) to find the answer. To see this consider u ( x , τ ) = c 1 ​ u ( 1 ) ( x , τ ) + c 2 ​ u ( 2 ) ( x , τ ) , where c 1 ​ and c 2 ​ are any constants. 笔记及习题解答：随机矩阵理论 · 导论 定义 0.1. Random Matrix 是取矩阵值的随机变量. 一个矩阵 A = ( a ij ​ ) 1 ≤ i , j ≤ n ​ , 其中每个元素 a ij ​ 均为随机变量或随机选择. 例 0.2 (对称随机矩阵) . 考虑对称阵 a ij ​ = a ji ​ , 且 a ij ​ ∈ { − 1 , 1 } . • 当 n = 1 时: 有 2 种矩阵. • 当 n = 2 时: 有 8 种矩阵. Stochastic Matrix 和 Random Matrix 不同, 某种意义上可以理解为随机过程中的转移矩阵. 1 研究对象与现象 研究对象主要是随机矩阵的 (奇异) 特征值、特征向量. • 半圆律 (Semicircle Law) : 对上述例子, 将特征值数值绘制成直方图, 在 N 很大时, 会出现规律. 当 N → ∞ , 经过适当尺度化 (scaling) 后, 特征值的密度函数趋向于 2 π 1 ​ 4 − x 2 ​ . • 普适性现象 (Universality) : 特征值的宏观极限规律不依赖于矩阵元素的具体分布. 例如, 无论 a ij ​ 是来自: ∘ { 1 , 2 , 3 , 4 } ∘ Gauss 分布 ∘ 其他独立同分布 只要限制矩阵的对称性以保证实特征值, 宏观现象是相似的. • 循环律 (Circular Law) : 对于非对称的复矩阵 G, 当 N → ∞ 时, 其特征值在复平面的单位圆内呈均匀分布. 2 Ulam 问题 定义 2.1. 令 S N ​ := { π ∣ π : { 1 , 2 , ... , N } → { 1 , 2 , ... , N }} 为 N 阶置换群 (permutation group). 对于一个置换 π ∈ S N ​ , 如果存在下标序列 1 ≤ i 1 ​ < i 2 ​ < ⋯ < i k ​ ≤ N 使得 π ( i 1 ​ ) < π ( i 2 ​ ) < ⋯ < π ( i k ​ ) , 则称序列 ( π ( i 1 ​ ) , … , π ( i k ​ )) 为一个长度为 k 的 增长子列 . L N ​ ( π ) 定义为 π 中 最长增长子列 的长度. 例 2.2. 对于 N = 5 , 置换 π : ( 1 , 2 , 3 , 4 , 5 ) → ( 5 , 1 , 3 , 2 , 4 ) . 其增长子列有 (1,3,4), (1,2,4) 等. 最长长度为 3, 即 L 5 ​ ( π ) = 3 . 在 S N ​ 上赋予均匀分布, 即 P ( π ) = N ! 1 ​ . 此时 L N ​ ( π ) : S N ​ → R 成为一个随机变量. 我们关心的问题是: 当 N → ∞ 时, L N ​ 的分布是什么? 定义 q n , N ​ := Prob ( L N ​ ( π ) ≤ n ) = N ! f n , N ​ ​ , 其中 f n , N ​ = # { π ∈ S N ​ ∣ L N ​ ( π ) ≤ n } . L N ​ 与下列问题有关 • S N ​ 的表示问题 (杨图, Young Tableaux). • 统计力学的粒子系统. • 首达渗流问题、增长模型、排斥过程. • 曲面上的随机拓扑. • 排序问题: 对 N 本编号为 1 N 的书进行排序, 需要操作的次数为 n = N − L N ​ ( π ) 次才能恢复原始排序. 历史 (History) • 1935 : Erdős-Szekeres, E ( L N ​ ) ≥ 2 1 ​ N − 1 ​ . • 1961 : Ulam 用蒙特卡洛方法, 猜测极限 lim N → ∞ ​ N ​ E ( L N ​ ) ​ = C 存在. • 1968 : Hammersley, 猜测 C = 2 . • 1972 : Logan-Shepp, 证明了极限存在. • 1977 : Vershik-Kerov, 证明了 C ≥ 2 , 从而确认了 C = 2 . • 1999 : Baik-Deift-Johansson, 证明了 L N ​ 的涨落分布: N 1/6 L N ​ − 2 N ​ ​ dist ​ χ 其中 χ 是 Tracy-Widom (TW) 分布, 该分布也描述了 GUE 随机矩阵最大特征值的分布.
